options: They are all identical with no functional differences
They differ in how money moves and what risks/limits apply to each
Only cards can be used for online shopping
Only wallets are regulated by any authority
questions.explanation:
Each method — UPI, net banking, cards, and wallets — moves money differently and carries its own specific risk profile,
limits, and regulatory framework.

questions.question: Why might a fraudster ask a victim to scan a QR code claiming it's for a "prize" or "cashback"?
options: Because scanning a QR code always results in receiving free money
Because this disguises an outgoing payment as if it were an incoming reward
Because QR codes can only be used for prizes
Because banks require QR scans for all cashback offers
questions.explanation:
Fraudulent "prize" or "cashback" QR scams exploit the false belief that scanning can bring in money, when it actually
authorises an outgoing payment.

questions.question: Which of these is an accurate statement about UPI fraud trends in India?
options: UPI fraud cases have completely disappeared in recent years
UPI fraud cases rose from about 6.32 lakh in FY2024-25 to around 10.64 lakh in FY2025-26 (till November)
UPI fraud only affects businesses, not individuals
UPI fraud cases are impossible to measure
questions.explanation:
Reported figures show a significant rise in UPI fraud cases even as the underlying technology remains secure, reflecting
growing social-engineering-based fraud.

questions.question: What is the safest way to verify a bank's customer care number?
options: Search for it casually on a general search engine
Check it directly on the bank's official app or website
Use the number provided in an unsolicited SMS
Ask a stranger for the number
questions.explanation:
Fraudulent customer care numbers frequently appear in search results or unsolicited messages; the bank's own official
app/website is the reliable source.

questions.question: What should you consider doing with a digital wallet you no longer actively use?
options: Keep maximum funds in it indefinitely
Transfer out the balance and consider closing the dormant wallet to reduce exposure
Share its login details with a friend for safekeeping
Increase its balance for convenience
questions.explanation:
Reducing balances in and closing dormant wallets you no longer use lowers your overall exposure if that app is ever
compromised.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of a "Prepaid Payment Instrument" (PPI)?
options: A type of credit card with no limit
A wallet or prepaid card where money is loaded in advance and spent later
A cheque book
A fixed deposit account
questions.explanation:
PPIs, like mobile wallets and prepaid cards, require loading money in advance before it can be spent, unlike direct bank
transfers.

questions.question: Which of these best represents responsible use of card controls offered by banking apps?
options: Enabling every feature (international, online, contactless) regardless of need
Enabling only the features you actually use, disabling the rest
Never checking or adjusting card controls at all
Sharing your card control settings publicly
questions.explanation:
Enabling only the card features you genuinely use limits the ways your card could be misused if the number were ever
compromised.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper notices, via CCTV, that a QR code payment sticker was tampered with. What real-world example does this
reflect?
options: A completely fictional scenario with no real basis
Documented QR code swap incidents where fraudulent codes replaced genuine ones at shops
A standard, harmless practice recommended by banks
A software bug in UPI apps
questions.explanation:
This reflects real, reported cases where fraudsters physically replaced QR codes at shops to redirect customer payments to
their own accounts.

questions.question:
Why is it recommended to check hospital or vendor identity independently rather than trusting a payment request
alone?
options: Because payment requests always indicate a genuine transaction
Because scammers can disguise fraudulent requests as legitimate-looking payment prompts
Because independent verification is illegal
Because banks forbid checking vendor identity
questions.explanation:
Verifying independently helps confirm that a payment request is genuine, rather than a disguised attempt to extract
money fraudulently.

questions.question: Which of these is the safest habit regarding your UPI PIN?
options: Share it with family members for convenience
Treat it exactly like your ATM PIN — never share it with anyone
Write it on the back of your phone case
Use the same UPI PIN as your social media password
questions.explanation:
Your UPI PIN authorises payments directly from your account, so it must be protected with the same seriousness as your
ATM PIN.

questions.question: What is the main reason online (card-not-present) transactions typically require an OTP?
options: To slow down the checkout process unnecessarily
Because such transactions carry higher fraud risk without physical card verification
Because OTPs are required only for cash transactions
Because online transactions are illegal without one
questions.explanation:
Since the card isn't physically verified in online transactions, an OTP adds a critical extra layer of authentication to reduce
fraud risk.

questions.question: What does "interoperability" mean in the context of digital wallets?
options: Wallets can only be used within a single app
A wallet's ability to work across multiple platforms/banks rather than being isolated to one provider
A wallet feature that disables all transactions
A wallet requirement for physical cash only
questions.explanation:
Interoperability allows a wallet to interact with other banks/platforms, which is an important factor when relying on a
wallet for larger transaction needs.

questions.question: Which government-regulated framework specifically addresses card tokenisation in India?
options: The Right to Information Act
The RBI Card Tokenisation Framework
The Consumer Protection Act
The Aadhaar Act
questions.explanation:
The RBI's Card Tokenisation Framework specifically mandates that merchants and apps store only encrypted tokens
instead of actual card details.

questions.question:
What is the best response if an unfamiliar "buyer" insists you must scan a code to complete a sale on an online
marketplace?
options: Comply immediately to finalise the sale
Decline and request a direct UPI ID transfer instead, since scanning to "receive" money is always a scam
Scan the code but close your eyes
Ask the buyer to scan your code instead
questions.explanation:
Since UPI never requires scanning to receive payment, declining and requesting a direct transfer avoids this well-
documented marketplace scam.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a "mule account" recruitment pattern?
options: A person knowingly and legally opens a business account

A person is recruited, sometimes unknowingly, to receive and quickly transfer fraudulent funds through their bank
account
A person opens a fixed deposit for retirement savings
A person applies for a standard personal loan
questions.explanation:
Mule accounts are often set up by recruiting individuals, sometimes without full awareness, to receive and move
fraudulently obtained money.

questions.question: What is the safest approach to receiving a large sum of money from an unfamiliar buyer for an online sale?
options: Immediately trust any payment confirmation screenshot sent by the buyer
Verify the actual credit in your own bank account or app before releasing goods
Release goods first and check payment later
Ask the buyer to scan a QR code you generate to "receive" from them
questions.explanation:
Screenshots can be faked; verifying the actual credit directly in your own account before completing a transaction avoids a
common scam.

questions.question: Why does RBI's 2FA mandate apply to both banks and non-bank payment providers?
options: Because non-bank providers don't handle real money
Because digital payment risk applies across the entire ecosystem, not just traditional banks
Because only banks are legally allowed to process payments
Because non-bank providers are exempt from all regulation
questions.explanation:
As payments increasingly flow through both banks and non-bank providers, RBI's authentication rules apply broadly to
protect the whole ecosystem.

questions.question: What should you do if your bank's app shows a transaction you don't recognise?
options: Ignore it if the amount is small
Report it to your bank immediately and check for a pattern of similar unauthorised activity
Delete the banking app to make the transaction disappear
Wait until your next statement to review it
questions.explanation:
Immediate reporting of any unrecognised transaction, regardless of size, helps limit further loss and supports timely fraud
investigation.

questions.question:
Which of these is a legitimate reason banks encourage customers to use their official mobile app over third-party sites
for banking?
options: Official apps are always slower
Official apps reduce exposure to phishing and fraudulent look-alike websites
Third-party sites are always more secure
There is no security difference between the two
questions.explanation:
Using the bank's official app avoids the risk of landing on a fraudulent look-alike website designed to steal login
credentials.

questions.question: What is a practical reason to periodically review which apps have access to your UPI or banking accounts?
options: Apps never retain access once granted
Unused or outdated app access can be a security risk if not periodically reviewed and revoked
Reviewing access is required only once in a lifetime
It has no security relevance at all
questions.explanation:
Periodically reviewing and revoking unnecessary app access reduces the number of potential points through which your
account could be compromised.

questions.question: What is the core lesson behind most successful UPI and card frauds in India?
options: UPI and card technology itself is fundamentally broken

Most frauds succeed by tricking users into an unnecessary action (like scanning or sharing a PIN), not by breaking the
technology
Only elderly citizens are ever targeted
Frauds only occur due to weak Wi-Fi signals
questions.explanation:
The core, recurring lesson is that fraud typically exploits user behaviour and trust, rather than any inherent flaw in UPI or
card security technology.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct definition of a "Fair Price Shop" in relation to payment/subsidy systems?
options: A shop offering the lowest prices on electronics
A shop distributing subsidised food grains under the Public Distribution System (unrelated to card payments)
A discount shop for banking products
A type of ATM✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
While not a payment method itself, understanding related terms like Fair Price Shops helps distinguish genuine
government service channels from payment fraud schemes exploiting similar names.

questions.question:
What action should you take if someone calls claiming to be a "bank employee" and asks you to install a remote-access
app to "fix an issue" with your account?
options: Install it immediately to resolve the issue quickly
Refuse — this is a known tactic used to gain control of your device and drain your accounts
Install it but only for five minutes
Ask them to email you the app link instead
questions.explanation:
Remote-access app requests from unsolicited callers are a well-known fraud tactic used to take control of a victim's device
and banking apps.

questions.question: What is the safest habit when receiving a "refund" notification for a purchase you don't recall making?
options: Click any link provided to claim the refund quickly
Verify independently through the official merchant or bank channel before taking any action
Share your card details to "confirm" the refund
Assume it's genuine since it mentions a specific amount
questions.explanation:
Fake refund notifications are a common fraud vector; independent verification through official channels avoids falling for
this scam.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a legitimate government initiative to protect digital payment users in India?
options: Removing all authentication requirements to speed up transactions
RBI's mandate for stronger digital payment authentication, effective April 2026
Eliminating UPI transaction limits entirely
Allowing merchants to store customer CVVs freely
questions.explanation:
RBI's 2025 Directions, requiring 2FA for digital payments from April 2026, reflect a deliberate regulatory effort to
strengthen payment security nationwide.

questions.question: Why is verifying the payee name before confirming a UPI transfer considered a best practice, even for small amounts?
options: Small amounts are never targeted by fraud
Errors or fraud can occur regardless of amount, and verification helps catch mistakes before they're irreversible
Payee names are never displayed in UPI apps
It is only relevant for business transactions
questions.explanation:
Since UPI transfers are typically instant and hard to reverse, verifying the payee name — regardless of transaction size —
helps prevent costly mistakes or fraud.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the most important overall principle for safe banking and payments?
options: Rely entirely on your bank to prevent every possible fraud automatically
Combine official channels, careful verification, and never sharing PINs/OTPs/CVVs with anyone
Avoid using digital payments altogether
Trust any message that mentions your bank's name
questions.explanation:
Safe banking relies on a combination of using official channels, verifying carefully before acting, and never sharing
sensitive authentication details with anyone.

questions.question: What do phishing, vishing, smishing, and fake job scams all have in common?
options: They only target businesses, never individuals
They are all forms of social engineering that manipulate people psychologically
They only work through email
They require advanced hacking skills to execute
questions.explanation:
All four scam types rely on manipulating human trust, fear, or greed rather than technically breaking into systems — the
defining trait of social engineering.

questions.question: What is "vishing"?
options: Phishing conducted via SMS
Phishing conducted via phone or video call
A type of antivirus software
A government helpline
questions.explanation:
Vishing is voice-based phishing, where scammers impersonate officials or bank staff over phone or video calls to extract
money or information.

questions.question: What is "smishing"?
options: Phishing conducted through SMS/text messages
A type of malware
A government scheme
Phishing conducted only through fax machines
questions.explanation: Smishing uses SMS messages, often about fake deliveries, KYC updates, or bills, to trick victims into clicking malicious links.

questions.question: Which of these is the most common psychological trigger scammers exploit in a "digital arrest" scam?
options: Curiosity
Fear
Boredom
Generosity✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
Digital arrest scams rely heavily on fear — falsely claiming the victim is under investigation to pressure them into
compliance.

questions.question: What is the defining pattern of a "task scam" targeting job seekers?
options: Victims are asked to pay upfront before any work begins, with no payment ever received
Victims are paid small amounts first to build trust, then asked to deposit larger sums to "unlock" bigger earnings
Victims receive a large salary immediately with no conditions
Victims are hired after a formal, lengthy interview process
questions.explanation:
Task scams deliberately pay small real amounts first to build false trust before demanding larger deposits, which are then
never returned.

questions.question:
According to a 2025 survey, approximately what percentage of WhatsApp users in India had received fraudulent job-
offer messages?
options: 15%✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
The 2025 survey found that 42% of WhatsApp users in India had encountered fraudulent job-offer messages, highlighting
how widespread this scam pattern has become.

questions.question: What does "spoofing" mean in the context of online scams?
options: Legitimately verifying a caller's identity
Disguising a caller ID, email address, or website to make it appear genuine
A type of antivirus scan
A method banks use to confirm transactions
questions.explanation: Spoofing lets scammers make a call, email, or website appear to come from a trusted source, even when it doesn't.

questions.question: What is a "look-alike domain"?
options: An official government website
A fake website URL designed to closely resemble a genuine one
A type of firewall setting
A verified secure payment gateway
questions.explanation:
Look-alike domains use subtle misspellings or extra words to mimic a genuine website, tricking users into entering
sensitive information.

questions.question: Why can modern phishing emails be difficult to identify by appearance alone?
options: They are always poorly written with obvious spelling errors
Modern phishing emails are often professionally designed and visually identical to genuine ones
Phishing emails never include any branding
They only ever come from unknown senders with random characters
questions.explanation:
Sophisticated phishing emails closely replicate a genuine brand's look and tone, meaning appearance alone is not a
reliable indicator of authenticity.

questions.question: Which of these is the safest way to verify an unexpected message claiming to be from your bank?
options: Click the link in the message directly
Go independently to the bank's official app or website, not through the message itself
Reply to the message asking if it's genuine
Call the number provided within the suspicious message
questions.explanation:
Verifying independently through official channels, rather than using contact details from the suspicious message itself,
avoids falling into the scammer's trap.

questions.question:
How many phishing domains did CERT-In's monitoring systems reportedly identify within billions of malicious DNS
queries analysed?
options: About 1,000
About 128 million
About 50
About 10,000✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
CERT-In's large-scale DNS analysis identified over 128 million phishing domains, reflecting the massive scale of phishing
infrastructure globally.

questions.question: Approximately how many cyber incidents did CERT-In handle in 2025?
options: About 10,000
About 29.44 lakh
About 500
About 2,000✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: CERT-In handled roughly 29.44 lakh cyber incidents in 2025, an increase of about 44% compared to 2024.

questions.question: What is the CISG-2025-02 guideline primarily focused on?
options: Banning all internet usage
Mandating annual third-party cybersecurity audits and structured breach reporting
Removing the need for passwords
Regulating television broadcasting
questions.explanation:
CISG-2025-02, effective July 2025, requires many digital entities to undergo regular third-party audits and follow structured
breach-reporting timelines.

questions.question: Which IT Act section specifically punishes "cheating by impersonation using a computer resource"?
options: Section 43
Section 66D
Section 67
Section 72✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
Section 66D covers cheating by impersonation through computer resources, forming the legal basis for prosecuting most
online scams.

questions.question:
A software engineer in Bengaluru reportedly lost around ₹43.48 lakh after a WhatsApp part-time job scam evolved into
what?
options: A genuine business partnership
A fraudulent cryptocurrency investment through a fake exchange link
A legitimate loan agreement
A government scheme registration
questions.explanation:
This widely reported case shows how task scams often escalate into larger fraudulent investment schemes once initial
trust has been established.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the five common psychological triggers scammers use?
options: Urgency
Authority
Software updates
Greed✅ Correct Answer: Option C
questions.explanation:
Software updates are a protective habit, not a manipulation tactic; scammers instead rely on urgency, fear, greed,
authority, and curiosity.

questions.question:
What should you do if a WhatsApp "recruiter" asks you to pay ₹2,000 to "unlock higher-paying tasks" after completing a
few paid tasks?
options: Pay immediately, since you've already been paid once
Recognise this as a task scam pattern and refuse to pay any further amount
Ask to double the payment first
Recommend the opportunity to friends immediately
questions.explanation: No legitimate job requires payment to access more work; this "unlock" request is a hallmark of the task scam pattern.

questions.question: Why do fraudsters in "digital arrest" scams often insist on keeping the victim on a continuous video call?
options: To provide entertainment during the call
To maintain psychological pressure and prevent the victim from pausing to verify the claim independently
Video calls are required for all police procedures
To improve call quality for legal reasons
questions.explanation:
Keeping the victim continuously engaged prevents them from stepping away to verify the claim, reinforcing the fear-
based pressure of the scam.

questions.question: What is the safest response to any "digital arrest" video call?
options: Comply with all instructions to avoid legal trouble
Disconnect immediately, since no genuine agency conducts arrests or investigations via video call
Ask the caller to email you further instructions
Transfer a small amount first to "test" the situation
questions.explanation:
No Indian law enforcement agency ever conducts an arrest, investigation, or fine collection through a video call —
disconnecting immediately is the correct response.

questions.question:
What percentage of surveyed users reported experiencing someone impersonating them on WhatsApp to scam their
own contacts?
options: 65%✅ Correct Answer: Option C
questions.explanation:
The same 2025 survey found that 12% of respondents had experienced impersonation of themselves used to scam their
own contacts.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why "urgency" is such an effective scam trigger?
options: It gives victims more time to think carefully
It pressures victims to act quickly, bypassing their normal instinct to verify and double-check
Urgency has no real psychological effect
It only works on people unfamiliar with technology
questions.explanation:
Creating urgency short-circuits careful thinking, pushing victims to act on instructions before they have a chance to verify
their legitimacy.

questions.question:
What is the correct action if you receive a message claiming your electricity will be disconnected tonight unless you
click a link and pay immediately?
options: Click the link and pay right away to avoid disconnection
Verify directly through your electricity board's official app or website
Forward the message to family to warn them, without verifying it yourself
Reply asking for a payment extension
questions.explanation:
This is a classic smishing pattern; verifying through the official utility provider's channel avoids falling for the fraudulent
urgent payment demand.

questions.question: Which of these best describes how educated professionals are affected by online scams?
options: They are always immune due to their education level

Educated professionals and senior citizens are frequently targeted and affected, since scams exploit psychology rather
than knowledge gaps
Only uneducated individuals are ever scammed
Education entirely eliminates scam risk
questions.explanation:
Since these scams exploit psychological triggers rather than technical knowledge, even highly educated professionals are
frequently and successfully targeted.

questions.question:
What is the recommended first step before reacting to any unexpected, urgent request related to money or personal
information?
options: Comply immediately to avoid any risk
Pause and verify the claim independently through an official channel
Ignore it completely without further thought
Ask a stranger online for advice
questions.explanation:
Pausing to verify independently is the single most effective countermeasure against nearly all forms of phishing, vishing,
and smishing.

questions.question: Which of these red flags is most associated with a fake job offer?
options: A formal interview process with a verifiable company
A request for an upfront "registration" or "training" fee before starting work
A written employment contract
Verification of company details through official channels
questions.explanation:
Legitimate employers never require candidates to pay upfront fees; such a request is one of the clearest signs of a fake job
offer.

questions.question: What role does "greed" play as a scam trigger?
options: It has no relevance to online scams
Offers of easy, high income for minimal effort exploit the desire for quick financial gain
It only applies to lottery scams specifically
It makes victims more cautious rather than less
questions.explanation: Promises of easy, high earnings for little effort exploit greed, making task scams and investment fraud especially effective.

questions.question: Which state recorded 395 task-fraud cases in a recent year, according to reported data?
options: Karnataka
Sikkim
Goa
Nagaland✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation:
Karnataka's reported task-fraud case data reflects how rapidly this scam category has grown, including a meaningful share
involving cryptocurrency schemes.

questions.question: What is the safest way to check if a "customer care" number found through a general internet search is genuine?
options: Trust it because it appeared at the top of the search results
Verify it against the number listed on the company's official app or website
Call it immediately without any further checking
Assume any number with the company name in the caller ID is genuine
questions.explanation: Fraudulent numbers frequently appear in search results; verifying against the official app or website is the reliable method.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why "authority" is an effective psychological trigger for scammers?
options: People are naturally suspicious of anyone claiming authority
People tend to comply more readily with instructions from perceived police, bank, or government officials
Authority figures never contact people by phone
It has no measurable effect on scam success rates
questions.explanation:
Impersonating police, bank officials, or government agents leverages people's natural tendency to comply with authority,
making scams more convincing.

questions.question: What is the best way to protect elderly family members from vishing scams?
options: Assume they already understand these risks without any discussion

Explain clearly that no genuine agency conducts arrests or demands money over a call, and encourage them to verify
independently
Disconnect their phone service entirely
Avoid discussing the topic to prevent worry
questions.explanation:
Clear, calm explanation of these scam patterns, along with encouraging independent verification, helps protect family
members who may be specifically targeted.

questions.question: Why do fraudsters often reference real, well-known companies in phishing and smishing messages?
options: To make the scam more believable by borrowing credibility from a trusted brand
Because real companies pay scammers to promote their brand
Because impersonating a real company is illegal and therefore avoided
It has no effect on the scam's success
questions.explanation:
Referencing a trusted, well-known brand lends false credibility to the scam, making victims less likely to question its
legitimacy.

questions.question: What should you do if you've already shared an OTP or personal details in response to a scam?
options: Do nothing, since it's already too late
Contact your bank immediately, change relevant passwords, and file a report at cybercrime.gov.in
Wait until the end of the month to check your statement
Share the same OTP again to confirm the transaction
questions.explanation:
Acting quickly — securing your accounts and reporting the incident — gives the best chance of limiting damage and
supporting recovery efforts.

questions.question: Which of these accurately reflects the growth of CERT-In's handled incidents between 2024 and 2025?
options: Incidents decreased by 44%
Incidents increased by about 44%, from 20.41 lakh to 29.44 lakh
There was no change at all
Incidents increased by only 2%
questions.explanation:
CERT-In's incident data shows a significant year-on-year rise, reflecting the growing scale and sophistication of online
scams.

questions.question: What is the safest way to respond to an SMS claiming your "KYC will expire today" with a link to click?
options: Click the link immediately to avoid account suspension
Ignore the link and verify your KYC status directly through your bank's official app or branch
Reply to the SMS with your account number
Forward the SMS to your bank's customer care number found in the message
questions.explanation:
Banks do not deactivate accounts through unsolicited text links; verifying through official channels avoids this common
smishing tactic.

questions.question: Which of these best captures the reason "curiosity" is used as a scam trigger?
options: Curious people are always more careful
Messages like "you have a pending parcel/refund — click to view" exploit natural curiosity to prompt risky clicks
Curiosity has no relevance to smishing or phishing
It only affects scams conducted via phone calls
questions.explanation:
Vague but intriguing messages about pending parcels or refunds exploit curiosity, prompting victims to click without
pausing to verify.

questions.question:
What does the "Cambridge Analytica" case, often referenced in discussions of online scams and data misuse, primarily
illustrate?
options: A purely fictional example with no real-world basis
How millions of users' data, harvested without proper consent, was reportedly used for political profiling
A case involving only Indian citizens
A case unrelated to third-party data sharing
questions.explanation:
The Cambridge Analytica case is a widely cited example of large-scale data harvesting without proper consent, raising
global awareness about third-party data sharing risks.

questions.question: Which of these is the most reliable way to identify a fraudulent job recruiter operating primarily over WhatsApp?
options: Trust them if they respond quickly to messages
Be cautious of hiring conducted entirely through informal messaging apps with no verifiable company channel
Assume all WhatsApp-based recruitment is automatically safe
Judge legitimacy purely by how professional their profile photo looks
questions.explanation:
Legitimate hiring usually involves verifiable, official channels; recruitment conducted solely through informal messaging
apps is a significant red flag.

questions.question: What is the primary reason scammers prefer disguising phishing attempts as urgent account security alerts?
options: Security alerts are always ignored by users
Urgency around account security makes victims act quickly without verifying, out of fear of losing access
Security alerts are illegal to send
It has no measurable impact on scam effectiveness
questions.explanation:
Fear of losing account access creates urgency, prompting hasty action — exactly the reaction phishing messages are
designed to trigger.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects appropriate caution when engaging with an online-only romantic or friendly relationship
that later asks for money?
options: Send money immediately to support someone you trust
Treat requests for money from someone you've never met in person with strong scepticism
Assume all online relationships are automatically scams
Share your bank details to build trust faster
questions.explanation:
Requests for money from an online-only relationship, especially one avoiding video calls or meetings, are a recognised
warning sign of romance-based fraud.

questions.question: What is a key reason phishing, vishing, and smishing are grouped together as related concepts?
options: They all require the same specific software to execute

They all share the underlying strategy of impersonating trust to manipulate victims, differing only in the
communication channel used
They only affect large corporations
They are entirely unrelated concepts
questions.explanation:
While the channel differs — email, call, or SMS — all three rely on the same core strategy of impersonating a trusted source
to manipulate the victim.

questions.question: Which of these is the safest practice when downloading an app recommended by an unknown online "job" contact?
options: Install it immediately since it was recommended
Avoid installing unknown apps recommended by unverified contacts, especially those tied to "task" platforms
Share your banking password to activate the app faster
Install it only on a friend's phone instead
questions.explanation: Unverified apps recommended through informal job/task contacts are frequently used to facilitate fraud or data theft.

questions.question:
What is the most effective way to protect yourself from being deceived by a highly convincing, professionally designed
phishing email?
options: Judge the email purely by its visual design and formatting
Independently verify sender details and links rather than relying on appearance alone
Trust any email that includes a company logo
Assume all professional-looking emails are automatically safe
questions.explanation:
Since appearance alone is unreliable, independently verifying the sender and any links is essential, regardless of how
professional an email looks.

questions.question: Which of the following best reflects the correct understanding of "sextortion" as a scam pattern?
options: It only involves financial fraud with no emotional manipulation

It typically combines fake relationships or compromising content with emotional or financial manipulation to extort
money
It is unrelated to social engineering
It exclusively targets business email accounts
questions.explanation:
Sextortion scams combine manipulation tactics — often built on a fabricated relationship — with threats to extort money
from victims.

questions.question: What should a person do upon realising they clicked a suspicious link but did not enter any personal information?
options: Assume there is no risk and take no further action
Monitor their device/accounts for unusual activity and consider running a security scan
Share the link with friends to warn them without further precaution
Restart their phone and consider the matter fully resolved
questions.explanation:
Even without entering data, clicking a malicious link can sometimes trigger downloads or redirects, so monitoring for
unusual activity is a sensible precaution.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why task scams are considered particularly deceptive compared to traditional upfront-fee
scams?
options: They ask for payment before any interaction occurs
They build genuine trust through real initial payouts before escalating to a larger, fraudulent ask
They never involve any real money changing hands
They are always immediately obvious to victims
questions.explanation:
By paying real, small amounts upfront, task scams disable the scepticism people typically apply to requests for payment,
making them especially deceptive.

questions.question: What is the safest way to handle an SMS from an unknown number offering "easy income" for minimal work?
options: Reply asking for more details about the opportunity
Treat it with caution, especially if it requests any payment or personal information
Forward your bank details to learn more
Assume it's genuine if it mentions a well-known company
questions.explanation:
Unsolicited "easy income" offers are a common scam pattern; treating any request for payment or personal data with
caution is essential.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects a safe organisational response to reduce large-scale phishing risk, according to CERT-In's
2025 guidelines?
options: Avoiding any cybersecurity audits to reduce cost
Conducting regular third-party cybersecurity audits and following structured breach-reporting timelines
Removing all customer data protection measures
Ignoring newly discovered vulnerabilities
questions.explanation:
CISG-2025-02 specifically mandates regular audits and structured reporting to help reduce the scale of exploitable
vulnerabilities that enable phishing infrastructure.

questions.question: What is the most reliable long-term defence against phishing, vishing, smishing, and fake job scams combined?
options: Relying entirely on antivirus software
Building a consistent habit of pausing and verifying independently before reacting to any unexpected urgent request
Avoiding phones and computers altogether
Trusting all messages that appear personalised
questions.explanation:
Since all four scam types exploit the same underlying pattern — a trigger, a fake authority, an urgent ask — consistently
pausing to verify is the most effective universal defence.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the relationship between "digital arrest" scams and vishing?
options: They are entirely unrelated categories
Digital arrest scams are a specific, prominent example of vishing, using voice/video calls to impersonate authority
Digital arrest scams only occur through email
Vishing never involves impersonating officials
questions.explanation:
Digital arrest scams are a widely reported form of vishing, where fraudsters use phone or video calls to impersonate police
or government officials.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the single most important takeaway about online scams in India?
options: They are rare and unlikely to affect most people
They succeed primarily by manipulating trust and urgency, and pausing to verify independently is the best defence
Only technically unsophisticated people are ever targeted
Avoiding smartphones entirely is the only real solution
questions.explanation:
The recurring lesson across phishing, vishing, smishing, and fake job scams is that they exploit psychological
manipulation, making independent verification the most powerful and universal defence.

questions.question: What does setting your Instagram account to "Private" primarily achieve?
options: It deletes all your previous posts
Only approved followers can see your posts and Stories
It makes your account visible to everyone automatically
It disables the app entirely
questions.explanation:
A private Instagram account restricts visibility of your posts and Stories to only the followers you've approved, reducing
exposure to strangers.

questions.question: What is a "catfish" account?
options: A verified celebrity account
A fabricated online identity used to build a fake relationship, often for manipulation
A government social media handle
An account used only for business marketing
questions.explanation:
Catfish accounts create an entirely false identity to build trust or emotional connection, often for financial or emotional
exploitation.

questions.question: What is "impersonation" in the context of fake profiles?
options: Creating an account using your own real name and photos
Creating a fake account using someone else's name or photos to deceive others
Verifying your identity through an official process
Reporting a suspicious account
questions.explanation: Impersonation accounts copy a real person's identity to deceive their contacts, often for scams or harassment.

questions.question: What is the most accurate definition of cyberbullying?
options: A single unpleasant comment on a post
A pattern of repeated harassment, humiliation, or threats carried out through digital platforms
Disagreeing with someone online once
Blocking an unwanted contact
questions.explanation:
Cyberbullying typically involves a sustained pattern of harmful behaviour, not a single isolated interaction, intended to
distress or control someone.

questions.question: According to a 2025 survey, what percentage of Indian teenagers reported experiencing cyberbullying?
options: 15%✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
The 2025 survey found 37% of Indian teens reported experiencing cyberbullying, among the highest rates recorded
globally.

questions.question: Under India's amended IT Rules, within how many hours must a platform acknowledge a user complaint?
options: 72 hours
24 hours
7 days
1 hour✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: The IT Rules require platforms to acknowledge user complaints within 24 hours, with a target resolution window of 15 days.

questions.question:
Under the amended IT Rules, within how many hours must content involving non-consensual intimate imagery be
taken down after a valid complaint?
options: 90 days
24 hours
1 year
6 months✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
Content involving nudity or non-consensual intimate imagery must be taken down within 24 hours of a valid complaint
under the amended IT Rules.

questions.question: What is "doxxing"?
options: Verifying someone's identity through official documents
Publicly revealing someone's private information without their consent
Blocking an account on social media
A method of encrypting messages
questions.explanation:
Doxxing involves exposing private details like someone's address or phone number publicly, often to harass or intimidate
them.

questions.question: What should you do BEFORE blocking or reporting an account that is harassing you?
options: Immediately delete all the messages
Save evidence, such as screenshots with timestamps and usernames
Reply angrily to the account first
Share your personal details to negotiate
questions.explanation: Preserving evidence before blocking ensures you have the necessary proof if you need to report the harassment formally.

questions.question: What is a "Significant Social Media Intermediary" (SSMI)?
options: Any account with more than 100 followers
A large platform meeting a government-notified user threshold, facing extra compliance obligations
A government department
A type of antivirus software
questions.explanation:
SSMIs are large platforms that must appoint a Chief Compliance Officer and Grievance Redressal Officer due to their scale
and reach.

questions.question: Which law provides special protection for children against sexual abuse and exploitation, including online?
options: The Consumer Protection Act
The POCSO Act, 2012
The Motor Vehicles Act
The Right to Information Act
questions.explanation:
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, provides dedicated legal protection for children,
including from online exploitation.

questions.question: Which IT Act section punishes capturing or publishing a person's private images without consent?
options: Section 66E
Section 43A
Section 8
Section 12✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation:
Section 66E specifically addresses violation of privacy through capturing or publishing images of a person's private activity
without consent.

questions.question: What is "trolling"?
options: Providing constructive, respectful feedback
Deliberately posting inflammatory or upsetting content to provoke a reaction
A method of verifying an account's authenticity
A privacy setting on Instagram
questions.explanation: Trolling involves intentionally provocative or upsetting posts made purely to elicit an emotional reaction from others.

questions.question: Which of these is a common sign of a fake profile?
options: A long-established account with years of consistent posting history
A very high follower-to-following ratio with only a few recent posts
Regular interaction with verified friends and family
A profile that matches information you've independently confirmed
questions.explanation:
Fake profiles often show a limited posting history combined with unusual follower patterns, unlike genuine, long-
established accounts.

questions.question: A profile using your friend's name and photos messages you urgently asking for money. What should you do?
options: Send the money immediately since it looks like your friend
Verify directly with your friend through a separate channel, like a phone call, before responding
Ask the profile for more personal details to confirm
Share your bank account number to "help" faster
questions.explanation:
This is a classic impersonation scam; verifying through an independent channel confirms whether the request is genuine
before taking any action.

questions.question: What is the safest way to handle repeated exclusion and mocking of your child in a class WhatsApp group?
options: Ignore it, assuming it will resolve on its own
Save evidence, involve the school and a trusted adult, and use the platform's reporting tools
Remove your child from all group chats permanently without further action
Confront the other parents publicly online
questions.explanation:
Documenting the harassment and involving both the school and formal reporting tools provides a structured, effective
response to cyberbullying involving a minor.

questions.question: Which of these platforms allows control over "last seen," profile photo, and status visibility under its privacy settings?
options: WhatsApp
A physical newspaper
A landline telephone
A television channel
questions.explanation: WhatsApp's privacy settings let users control who can see their last seen status, profile photo, and status updates.

questions.question: What is a key risk specific to large public groups/channels on Telegram?
options: They are always heavily moderated
They often have minimal moderation, increasing exposure to scams and unfamiliar links
They cannot be joined by strangers
They automatically verify all members' identities
questions.explanation:
Large public Telegram groups often lack strong moderation, making them a common venue for spam, scams, and
harmful content.

questions.question: What does "Restrict" or "Block" on Instagram help achieve?
options: It permanently deletes the other user's account
It limits or stops unwanted interaction from a specific account
It reports the account to the police automatically
It makes your own account private
questions.explanation:
"Restrict" and "Block" are tools that let you limit or cut off interaction from unwanted accounts without necessarily
escalating further.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of a "Grievance Officer" under India's IT Rules?
options: A police officer specialising in cybercrime
A platform representative required to acknowledge and resolve user complaints
A social media influencer
A government minister overseeing all platforms
questions.explanation:
Platforms are required to designate a Grievance Officer responsible for handling and resolving user complaints within
specified timelines.

questions.question:
Which of these is the safest response to an anonymous account repeatedly posting embarrassing comments about a
coworker in a public group?
options: Ignore it completely with no action

Report the account and specific posts to the platform, and encourage the affected person to document and report
formally
Post similar comments about the anonymous account in retaliation
Ask the coworker to leave the group instead
questions.explanation:
Formal reporting, combined with documentation, is more effective and appropriate than retaliation or simply hoping the
harassment stops.

questions.question: What is a common sign of a catfishing relationship?
options: The person is always willing to video call
The person consistently avoids video calls despite claiming a close relationship
The relationship involves verified, in-person meetings
The person shares consistent, verifiable personal details
questions.explanation: A persistent unwillingness to video call, despite claiming closeness, is a classic warning sign of a fabricated online identity.

questions.question: What does the IT Rules' 36-hour takedown timeline specifically apply to?
options: Any post with fewer than 10 likes
Content subject to a valid court or government order
All content posted before 2020
Only content in regional languages
questions.explanation: The 36-hour timeline applies to content that a court or government order has directed platforms to remove.

questions.question: Why should evidence be gathered BEFORE blocking a harassing account, rather than after?
options: Blocking automatically deletes all evidence of the interaction
Once blocked, you may lose easy access to view or screenshot the harassing content
Blocking is illegal without prior evidence
There is no real reason; order doesn't matter
questions.explanation:
Blocking can limit your ability to revisit and document the harassing content, so gathering evidence first is a
recommended best practice.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)?
options: Managing India's postal services
Addressing child-safety concerns, including online harassment and exploitation involving minors
Regulating banking transactions
Issuing passports
questions.explanation:
NCPCR is the statutory body focused specifically on protecting children's rights, including in matters of online safety and
exploitation.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects safe practice regarding location tagging on social media posts?
options: Always tag your exact live location for authenticity
Turn off precise location tagging, especially on public posts
Share your home address in your bio for convenience
Location tagging has no privacy implications
questions.explanation: Turning off precise location tagging reduces the risk of your movements and whereabouts being tracked by strangers.

questions.question:
What is the recommended action if an account claims to be a well-known celebrity offering a "giveaway" requiring a
small upfront payment?
options: Pay immediately to avoid missing the giveaway
Recognise this as a common impersonation scam pattern and avoid engaging
Share your bank details to "verify" eligibility
Assume all celebrity accounts are automatically genuine
questions.explanation:
Fake celebrity or brand giveaway accounts requesting payment are a widely reported and persistent impersonation scam
pattern.

questions.question: What is a "bot/spam account" typically used for?
options: Genuine, personal social interaction only
Automated or low-effort activity used to spread scams, spam, or fake engagement
Official government communication exclusively
Verified news reporting
questions.explanation:
Bot and spam accounts are typically automated or minimally maintained, used to spread scams or artificially inflate
engagement.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of escalation recommended for handling a fake profile impersonating you?
options: Confront the account publicly first, then consider reporting later
Report the account using the platform's official tools, then inform friends/family and escalate further if necessary
Delete your own account immediately without taking any other action
Share your ID proof with the fake account to "prove" your identity
questions.explanation:
Using the platform's official reporting tools, followed by informing your contacts, is the recommended structured response
to impersonation.

questions.question: What does "SSMI" status typically require a large platform to appoint, according to India's IT Rules?
options: A Chief Compliance Officer and Grievance Redressal Officer
A national security advisor
A government-appointed CEO
No additional appointments are required
questions.explanation:
Significant Social Media Intermediaries must appoint specific compliance and grievance-handling officers due to their
scale and impact.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a healthy family approach to children's social media use?
options: Avoiding all discussion of online experiences to prevent worry

Maintaining open, non-judgmental conversation about online experiences and learning platform reporting tools
together
Allowing unrestricted, unsupervised access with no guidance
Banning all internet access permanently
questions.explanation:
Open conversation combined with practical knowledge of reporting tools equips families to respond effectively to online
risks facing children.

questions.question: What is the correct response if cyberbullying involves threats or sharing of private images without consent?
options: Treat it as a minor issue requiring no formal reporting
Treat it as serious, requiring immediate reporting to the platform and the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
Handle it only through private conversation with the bully
Wait to see if it happens again before taking any action
questions.explanation:
Threats or non-consensual image sharing are serious matters requiring formal, immediate reporting rather than informal
resolution attempts.

questions.question: Which government ministry administers the IT Rules governing social media platforms in India?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
Ministry of Railways
Ministry of Agriculture
Ministry of Textiles
questions.explanation: MeitY is the ministry responsible for administering the IT Rules that govern social media intermediaries operating in India.

questions.question: What is the main risk of accepting follow/friend requests from unfamiliar accounts without verification?
options: There is no real risk if your account is private
It can expose you to impersonation, scams, or unwanted contact from unverified sources
It automatically improves your account's security
It is required to use social media at all
questions.explanation: Accepting unverified requests increases exposure to scams, impersonation attempts, and potentially harmful contact.

questions.question:
What should you check before trusting a long-distance online relationship that consistently avoids meeting or video
calling?
options: Nothing — persistent avoidance is completely normal
Treat repeated avoidance of verification (like video calls) as a red flag for catfishing
Send money to build trust faster
Share your home address to encourage them to visit
questions.explanation:
Persistent avoidance of video calls or meetings despite claims of closeness is one of the clearest indicators of a catfishing
scenario.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the purpose of platform-specific "Report" tools?
options: To permanently silence any account you disagree with
To formally flag content or accounts for violating platform policies, such as harassment or impersonation
To automatically alert the police in every case
To increase your own follower count
questions.explanation:
Report tools are the official mechanism for flagging policy-violating content or accounts, distinct from informal complaints
or confrontation.

questions.question: What does the term "cyberbullying" NOT typically include?
options: Repeated hurtful comments over time
A single, isolated disagreement resolved amicably between two people
Exclusion from group chats as an ongoing pattern
Spreading rumours online repeatedly
questions.explanation:
Cyberbullying is generally characterised by a repeated pattern of harm, distinguishing it from a single disagreement that is
resolved without lasting harm.

questions.question: Which of these actions best reflects "digital footprint" awareness on social media?
options: Posting your daily routine and travel plans publicly
Being mindful of what personal details are shared, even in seemingly harmless posts
Sharing your phone number publicly for convenience
Assuming nothing you post can ever be traced back to you
questions.explanation:
Being mindful of what you share, understanding it can persist and be traced, reflects responsible awareness of your digital
footprint.

questions.question: What is the recommended response if you discover an old, unused social media account you no longer need?
options: Leave it active indefinitely with default settings
Review its privacy settings, remove unnecessary personal data, or deactivate/delete it if unused
Share the login details publicly since it's no longer important
Increase its visibility to attract more followers
questions.explanation:
Unused accounts can still expose personal data or be exploited if compromised, so reviewing or removing them reduces
unnecessary risk.

questions.question: Which of these best describes why platforms are legally required to have a Grievance Officer in India?
options: To ensure complaints are ignored efficiently
To ensure user complaints are acknowledged and addressed within defined legal timelines
Because it is an optional courtesy with no legal basis
To replace the need for any government oversight
questions.explanation:
The Grievance Officer requirement is a legal obligation under the IT Rules, ensuring user complaints receive a structured,
timely response.

questions.question: What is the best way to teach a family member to recognise a fake profile?
options: Tell them all social media accounts are equally trustworthy
Teach them to check posting history, follower ratios, and be cautious of urgent money/personal requests
Advise them to accept every request to avoid seeming rude
Tell them fake profiles only exist on certain platforms
questions.explanation:
Understanding common red flags — limited posting history, unusual ratios, urgent requests — helps family members
independently spot fake profiles.

questions.question:
Which of these is an appropriate response to receiving unwanted, repeated messages from a stranger despite blocking
attempts?
options: Assume nothing more can be done after blocking once
Report the pattern formally to the platform and, if serious, to law enforcement or cybercrime authorities
Reply with personal information to try to make them stop
Create a new account to avoid the issue instead of reporting it
questions.explanation:
Persistent unwanted contact, especially after blocking, warrants formal reporting to the platform and potentially law
enforcement, rather than simply avoiding it.

questions.question: What is the safest way to verify if a photo used in a suspicious profile might be fake or stolen?
options: Assume all photos posted online are guaranteed genuine
Consider using a reverse image search where possible, and treat unverifiable profiles with caution
Message the profile asking them to confirm it's real
There is no way to check this at all
questions.explanation:
Reverse image checking and general caution toward unverifiable profiles help identify accounts using stolen or fake
photos.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a responsible approach to sharing content about children on social media?
options: Regularly posting identifiable details like school name and location
Avoiding posting identifiable details of children, such as their school or precise location, publicly
Sharing children's full daily schedules publicly for family updates
There are no privacy concerns when posting about children
questions.explanation:
Avoiding identifiable details like school names or locations helps protect children from potential exploitation or unwanted
contact.

questions.question: What should be your first reaction upon discovering that someone has created a fake account impersonating you?
options: Ignore it completely, assuming it will resolve itself
Use the platform's impersonation reporting category and inform close contacts who might be targeted
Create multiple accounts to compete with the fake one
Publicly share personal documents to "prove" the fake account is not you
questions.explanation:
Reporting through the platform's specific impersonation category, combined with alerting your contacts, is the most
effective initial response.

questions.question: Which of these best describes appropriate use of "Restrict" features versus outright blocking on social platforms?
options: There is no functional difference between the two
Restrict can limit unwanted interaction with less confrontation, while blocking cuts off contact entirely
Restrict permanently deletes the other account
Blocking is always the wrong choice regardless of severity
questions.explanation:
Restrict offers a subtler way to limit unwanted interaction, while blocking is a more definitive cutoff — both are legitimate
tools depending on the situation's severity.

questions.question: Why is it important to distinguish between "trolling" and more serious "cyberbullying"?
options: There is no meaningful distinction between the two

Trolling may be a single provocative act, while cyberbullying typically reflects a sustained, harmful pattern requiring
more serious response
Trolling is always more serious than cyberbullying
Only cyberbullying is ever punishable under law
questions.explanation:
Recognising the difference helps determine the appropriate response — from simple reporting for isolated trolling to
formal escalation for sustained cyberbullying.

questions.question:
What should employers or schools ideally align their cybersecurity/social-media awareness sessions with, as a general
best practice?
options: No particular schedule is beneficial
A regular, recurring cadence, reinforcing awareness rather than a single one-time session
Only new employee/student orientation, never repeated
Random, unannounced sessions with no consistent theme
questions.explanation:
Recurring, scheduled awareness sessions reinforce safe habits over time, rather than relying on a single session that
awareness may fade from.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the relationship between fake profiles and financial fraud?
options: Fake profiles are never used for financial scams
Impersonation and catfish accounts are frequently used as a vehicle to build trust before committing financial fraud
Financial fraud only occurs through email, never social media
Fake profiles are exclusively used for harmless pranks
questions.explanation:
Many financial scams begin with a fake profile building trust with the victim before requesting money or sensitive
information.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the most important overall principle for social media safety?
options: Trust every profile and message that appears genuine at first glance
Verify the person or account independently, document harm before reporting, and never face serious harassment alone
Avoid using social media entirely to eliminate all risk
Assume platforms have no legal obligation to respond to complaints
questions.explanation:
Independent verification, evidence-based reporting, and seeking support for serious harassment together form the
foundation of safe social media use.

questions.question: What is Google Play Protect?
options: A paid antivirus subscription service
Android's built-in malware-scanning system that runs continuously in the background
A government cybersecurity agency
A type of mobile data plan
questions.explanation:
Google Play Protect is Android's built-in, free protection system that continuously scans installed and newly downloaded
apps for threats.

questions.question: Approximately how many apps does Google Play Protect scan daily?
options: About 1,000
Over 350 billion
About 500
About 10 million
questions.explanation:
Google Play Protect scans over 350 billion apps daily, reflecting the massive scale of Android's built-in security
infrastructure.

questions.question: What is "sideloading" in the context of Android apps?
options: Installing an app directly from the Google Play Store
Installing an app from outside the official app store
Updating an app automatically
Deleting an app permanently
questions.explanation: Sideloading means installing apps from sources outside the Play Store, bypassing its security review process.

questions.question: Why is sideloading considered risky?
options: It uses significantly more mobile data than normal
It bypasses the Play Store's security review, making it a leading source of new Android malware
It automatically improves device performance
It has no real security implications
questions.explanation:
Since sideloaded apps skip Google's official review process, they were the dominant source of new Android malware
detected in 2025.

questions.question: When did Windows 10 reach the end of standard support?
options: 14 October 2025
1 January 2026
14 October 2020
31 December 2025
questions.explanation:
Windows 10 reached the end of standard support on 14 October 2025, after which routine security patches are no longer
automatically provided.

questions.question: Until when do free consumer Extended Security Updates (ESU) for Windows 10 run?
options: Indefinitely, with no end date
13 October 2026
14 October 2025
1 January 2030
questions.explanation:
Free consumer ESU for Windows 10 provides critical security patches only until 13 October 2026, after which unsupported
devices remain unpatched.

questions.question: What is Microsoft Defender?
options: A third-party paid antivirus exclusive to businesses
Windows' built-in antivirus and firewall protection, enabled by default
A government cybersecurity policy
A web browser
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender is Windows' free, built-in security solution that provides antivirus and firewall protection automatically.

questions.question: What is the difference between a "security patch" and a "feature update"?
options: There is no meaningful difference
A security patch fixes a specific vulnerability, while a feature update adds new functionality
Feature updates always fix security issues, and patches add new features
Security patches are optional and never necessary
questions.explanation:
A security patch specifically addresses a known vulnerability, whereas a feature update focuses on new functionality or
design changes.

questions.question: What is a "runtime permission" on Android?
options: A permission that never expires or can be changed
An app's request for access to a specific feature, like camera or location, at the moment it's needed
A type of malware
A setting that disables all app functionality
questions.explanation:
Runtime permissions let apps request access to specific features only when needed, and users can grant, deny, or later
revoke that access.

questions.question: A flashlight app requests access to your contacts and SMS messages. What should you do?
options: Grant the permissions since flashlight apps always need this access
Deny the request, since a flashlight app has no legitimate need for contacts or SMS
Uninstall your phone's operating system
Share the permissions with a friend for verification
questions.explanation:
A flashlight app has no functional need for contacts or SMS access; such a request is a clear red flag for over-collection of
data.

questions.question: What is the "principle of least privilege"?
options: Granting every app maximum access by default
Granting only the minimum access an app genuinely needs to function
A rule that applies only to government employees
A feature that disables all app permissions permanently
questions.explanation:
The principle of least privilege means apps and users should only be granted the access strictly necessary for their
intended function.

questions.question: What recent Android feature helps prevent social-engineering scams that try to get users to disable protection?
options: Android now allows disabling Play Protect at any time with one tap
Android prevents disabling Play Protect while the user is on an active phone call
Android has removed Play Protect entirely
There is no such feature
questions.explanation:
This feature directly targets scams where fraudsters try to talk victims into disabling protection during a call before
installing malicious software.

questions.question: How many new malicious apps from outside the Play Store did Google reportedly detect in 2025?
options: About 27 million, up from 13 million in 2024
About 100
About 5,000
About 1 million, down from 27 million
questions.explanation:
Detections of malicious apps from outside the Play Store roughly doubled in 2025 compared to 2024, highlighting the
growing sideloading risk.

questions.question: What does antivirus software primarily protect against?
options: Voluntarily shared passwords and OTPs
Malicious software and known threat signatures
Poor Wi-Fi signal strength
Slow typing speed
questions.explanation:
Antivirus software is designed to detect and block malicious code; it cannot prevent a user from voluntarily giving away
sensitive information to a scammer.

questions.question: What is TPM (Trusted Platform Module), relevant to Windows 11's requirements?
options: A type of antivirus subscription
A hardware security chip supporting encryption and secure boot processes
A government regulatory body
A software feature unrelated to security
questions.explanation:
TPM is a hardware chip that enables stronger security features like encryption and secure boot, forming part of Windows
11's baseline requirements.

questions.question: What does "Secure Boot" ensure?
options: That a device charges faster
That only trusted software loads when a device starts up
That Wi-Fi connects automatically
That antivirus software is disabled by default
questions.explanation:
Secure Boot verifies that only trusted, signed software is allowed to run during the startup process, protecting against
certain low-level malware.

questions.question: What is the Cyber Swachhta Kendra?
options: A paid antivirus company
A CERT-In initiative providing free malware-removal tools to Indian citizens
A government tax portal
A mobile network provider
questions.explanation:
Cyber Swachhta Kendra is a CERT-In initiative offering free malware-detection and removal tools, with reported coverage
across roughly 98% of India's digital population.

questions.question: Why should you avoid installing pirated or cracked versions of paid software?
options: Pirated software always performs better than genuine versions
It commonly requires disabling security checks, making it a frequent vector for malware
Pirated software is always completely safe if downloaded from a popular site
There is no relationship between piracy and malware risk
questions.explanation:
Installing cracked software often requires bypassing normal security protections, which criminals exploit to distribute
malware.

questions.question: What should you do if your browser warns that a download may be harmful?
options: Ignore the warning and proceed, since warnings are usually false alarms
Take the warning seriously and verify the source before proceeding
Disable browser warnings permanently
Share the download link with others immediately
questions.explanation:
Browser download warnings are based on threat intelligence and should prompt careful verification rather than being
dismissed.

questions.question: Which of the following best reflects safe practice regarding app permissions over time?
options: Grant permissions once and never review them again
Periodically review and revoke permissions that are no longer necessary
Assume all previously granted permissions remain appropriate forever
Only review permissions if your phone stops working
questions.explanation:
Apps and their needs change over time, so periodically reviewing and revoking unnecessary permissions is an important
ongoing security habit.

questions.question:
What happens to a device's security posture if it continues running an unsupported operating system without any
mitigation?
options: Nothing changes; unsupported devices remain fully protected
Newly discovered vulnerabilities remain permanently unpatched, increasing risk over time
The device automatically upgrades itself for free
Antivirus software becomes unnecessary
questions.explanation:
Without security updates, any new vulnerabilities discovered after support ends remain exploitable indefinitely on that
device.

questions.question: What is a "patch," specifically?
options: A cosmetic redesign of an app's interface
An update that fixes a specific security vulnerability
A type of malware
A hardware component inside a phone
questions.explanation: A patch specifically targets and fixes a known security vulnerability, distinct from broader feature updates.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why attackers specifically target devices that have delayed installing updates?
options: Updated devices are always easier to hack
Delayed devices retain known, exploitable vulnerabilities that a patch would have already fixed
Attackers cannot target updated devices under any circumstances
Update status has no bearing on device vulnerability
questions.explanation:
Attackers often specifically exploit known vulnerabilities that remain unpatched on devices where updates have been
delayed or ignored.

questions.question: What is the safest source for downloading a new mobile app?
options: A link shared via WhatsApp by an unknown contact
The official app store (such as Google Play)
A random third-party download website
An APK file attached to an unsolicited email
questions.explanation:
Official app stores conduct security reviews before listing apps, making them significantly safer than unofficial or
unsolicited sources.

questions.question: How many risky sideload/installation attempts did Google Play Protect reportedly block in 2025?
options: About 1,000
About 266 million
About 50
About 5 million
questions.explanation:
Google Play Protect blocked roughly 266 million risky sideload attempts in 2025, reflecting the scale of protection against
unofficial app installations.

questions.question: What is the correct action if you no longer use a particular app on your phone?
options: Leave it installed indefinitely with all its permissions intact
Uninstall it, rather than leaving it with standing permissions
Grant it additional permissions for future use
Share it with friends before removing it
questions.explanation: Uninstalling unused apps removes unnecessary standing permissions and reduces your overall device's attack surface.

questions.question: Which of these best represents a legitimate reason to disable a specific app permission?
options: The app clearly needs that permission to perform its stated core function
The permission requested has no clear connection to the app's actual purpose
The app is very popular
The app was recently updated
questions.explanation: Permissions unrelated to an app's core function are a warning sign and generally should be denied or revoked.

questions.question: What is one advantage of keeping automatic updates enabled for your operating system and apps?
options: It disables all app functionality
It ensures known security vulnerabilities are patched promptly without requiring manual action
It slows your phone down permanently
It removes the need for any other security measure
questions.explanation:
Automatic updates ensure you receive security patches as soon as they're released, minimising the window of
vulnerability.

questions.question: Why can't antivirus software prevent an OTP-sharing scam?
options: Antivirus software actually can prevent this type of scam directly
OTP-sharing scams rely on social engineering, which targets human behaviour rather than malicious code
Antivirus software is designed specifically to stop OTP scams
OTP scams do not exist in reality
questions.explanation:
Since these scams manipulate a person into voluntarily sharing information, no malware-focused tool like antivirus
software can prevent it.

questions.question: What is the correct order of steps to check for updates on an Android device?
options: Settings → System → Software Update → Check for updates
Contacts → Call → Update
Camera → Gallery → Update
There is no way to manually check for Android updates
questions.explanation: This is the standard path on most Android devices to manually check for and install available system updates.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a "red flag" permission request?
options: A messaging app requesting access to contacts
A simple calculator app requesting access to your location and camera
A camera app requesting access to your camera
A maps app requesting access to your location
questions.explanation:
A calculator app has no legitimate functional need for location or camera access, making such a request a clear warning
sign.

questions.question: How many policy-violating apps did Google reportedly block from the Play Store in 2025?
options: About 1.75 million
About 10
About 100✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation:
Google blocked around 1.75 million policy-violating apps from the Play Store in 2025 as part of its ongoing security
enforcement.

questions.question: What should you do before selling or discarding a computer or phone?
options: Simply delete a few personal files
Perform a full factory reset and remove linked accounts to protect residual personal data
Nothing; new owners cannot access old data by default
Give it away immediately without any preparation
questions.explanation:
A full factory reset combined with removing linked accounts helps ensure your personal data isn't accessible to the next
owner.

questions.question: Which of these best describes CISG-2025-02?
options: A new mobile operating system
CERT-In guidelines mandating regular third-party cybersecurity audits for many digital service providers
A type of antivirus software
A banking regulation unrelated to cybersecurity
questions.explanation:
CISG-2025-02 strengthens organisational cybersecurity by requiring regular audits and structured breach reporting from
many digital entities.

questions.question: What is the safest response to a pop-up claiming "Your device is infected, click here to fix it now"?
options: Click the pop-up immediately to resolve the issue
Treat it with suspicion, close it, and check your device using a trusted, official security tool instead
Share the pop-up with friends to warn them
Restart your device and ignore any further checks
questions.explanation:
Such alarming pop-ups are frequently themselves a scam tactic; verifying through trusted, official tools avoids falling for a
fake "fix."

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the relationship between updates and vulnerabilities?
options: Nearly every major cyberattack exploits a vulnerability for which a patch already existed
Updates have no relationship to reducing cyberattack risk
Only very old devices can ever be attacked
Vulnerabilities disappear automatically over time without any patch
questions.explanation:
Most significant cyberattacks specifically target vulnerabilities that already have an available patch, which is why prompt
updating matters so much.

questions.question: What did Google report about apps stopped from over-accessing user data in 2025?
options: Over 255,000 apps were stopped from over-accessing user data
No apps were ever found over-accessing data
Only 5 apps were affected
This figure is unrelated to Android security efforts
questions.explanation:
Google reported stopping over 255,000 apps from over-accessing user data in 2025, reflecting ongoing enforcement
against excessive data collection.
