questions.question: What is the safest approach when a stranger on a call asks you to disable your phone's security feature to "fix an issue"?
options: Comply immediately since the caller claims to be helping
Refuse — this matches a known social-engineering tactic to disable protection before installing malware
Disable the feature but re-enable it after five minutes
Ask the caller to email you instructions instead
questions.explanation:
Requests to disable security protections during an unsolicited call are a recognised scam tactic and should always be
refused.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate device security practice for families?
options: Assume children and seniors already understand these concepts without guidance
Set up devices with automatic updates enabled by default and review installed apps/permissions together periodically
Avoid discussing device security with family members entirely
Disable all security features for convenience
questions.explanation:
Proactively setting up automatic updates and periodically reviewing apps together helps extend good device security
habits across the whole family.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of "device security" as covered in this module?
options: Only relates to antivirus software
Protection resting on the operating system, updates, antivirus, app permissions, and safe habits together
A term with no practical application
Exclusively a concern for businesses, not individuals
questions.explanation:
Device security is a combination of several pillars working together — OS protections, timely updates, antivirus, careful
permissions, and safe habits.

questions.question: Why might seasonal spikes in fake shopping or discount apps occur around major shopping periods?
options: Seasonal apps are always safer than regular apps

Scammers exploit high shopping activity by creating fake apps that often request excessive permissions or contain
malware
There is no correlation between shopping seasons and malicious apps
Only genuine retailers create apps during shopping seasons
questions.explanation:
Security researchers have observed recurring spikes in malicious shopping/discount apps timed to exploit high consumer
activity during shopping seasons.

questions.question: What does "over-accessing user data" mean in the context of app behaviour?
options: An app requesting and using more data/permissions than necessary for its function
An app using exactly the data it needs and no more
A government policy on data limits
A feature that improves app performance
questions.explanation:
Over-accessing occurs when an app collects more user data than its actual function requires, which platforms like Google
actively work to detect and stop.

questions.question: Which factor most directly explains why Windows 11 requires TPM and Secure Boot as baseline requirements?
options: To make installation more complicated for no reason
To raise the overall security baseline through stronger hardware-based protections
TPM and Secure Boot have no connection to security
To prevent any updates from ever being installed
questions.explanation:
These requirements are specifically intended to strengthen device security through hardware-backed encryption and
startup verification.

questions.question: What is the recommended response to an app requesting permissions that seem unrelated to its stated function?
options: Grant the permissions anyway since the app is likely trustworthy
Deny the request or consider avoiding the app altogether
Report the app to your internet service provider only
Assume all apps in the Play Store request only necessary permissions
questions.explanation:
Unrelated permission requests are a warning sign, and denying them (or avoiding the app) helps limit unnecessary data
exposure.

questions.question: Which best reflects why fake APK files shared via WhatsApp have been a persistent issue in India?
options: WhatsApp has no relationship to app distribution
Fraudulent APKs disguised as courier, government, or utility apps exploit trust and bypass Play Store review
APK files cannot contain malware
WhatsApp automatically screens all shared files for malware
questions.explanation:
Fraudulent APKs shared through WhatsApp, often disguised as legitimate services, remain a common trojan-delivery
method precisely because they skip official review.

questions.question: What is the correct relationship between "antivirus" and "safe habits" in an overall device security strategy?
options: Antivirus alone is sufficient; safe habits are unnecessary
Both are necessary; antivirus addresses malware, while safe habits address human-targeted risks like scams
Safe habits alone are sufficient; antivirus is unnecessary
They serve identical purposes with complete overlap
questions.explanation:
Antivirus and safe habits address different categories of risk — malicious code versus manipulated human behaviour —
making both necessary together.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects good practice regarding Windows Update settings?
options: Disable Windows Update permanently to avoid interruptions
Leave Windows Update enabled on automatic to receive security patches promptly
Only check for updates once a year
Updates should always be postponed indefinitely
questions.explanation:
Keeping Windows Update on automatic ensures timely delivery of critical security patches without requiring manual
intervention.

questions.question: What happened to detections of malicious apps from outside the Play Store between 2024 and 2025?
options: They remained exactly the same
They roughly doubled, rising from about 13 million to about 27 million
They decreased significantly
They dropped to zero
questions.explanation:
The near-doubling of detected malicious apps from outside the Play Store highlights the growing risk associated with
sideloading.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct approach to a Windows 10 device nearing the end of its ESU coverage?
options: Ignore it completely with no plan
Plan an upgrade to a supported Windows version, or confirm ESU enrollment status before support ends
Assume the device will remain secure indefinitely regardless of ESU status
Switch to an unrelated, unsupported operating system as a solution
questions.explanation:
Proactively planning an upgrade or confirming ESU enrollment prevents a device from being left without critical security
patches once support fully ends.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, which statement best summarises effective device security?
options: A single strong antivirus product guarantees complete protection on its own
Effective device security combines updated software, trusted app sources, careful permissions, and safe habits together
Device security is irrelevant if you don't use online banking
Only businesses need to worry about device security, not individuals
questions.explanation:
No single tool is sufficient alone; genuine device security comes from combining updates, trusted sources, mindful
permissions, and consistent safe habits.

questions.question: What does HTTPS confirm about a website connection?
options: That the website itself is completely trustworthy
That the connection between your browser and the site is encrypted
That the website has no advertisements
That the website is government-owned
questions.explanation:
HTTPS confirms only that the connection is encrypted; it does not guarantee that the website itself is genuine or
trustworthy.

questions.question: Can a fake, fraudulent website use HTTPS?
options: No, fake websites can never use HTTPS
Yes, fake websites can and often do use HTTPS too
HTTPS is illegal for fraudulent websites
HTTPS is only available to government websites
questions.explanation:
Fraudulent websites frequently use HTTPS to appear more legitimate, which is why the padlock icon alone cannot confirm
authenticity.

questions.question: What is "typosquatting"?
options: A method of encrypting website traffic
Registering a domain based on a common misspelling of a genuine website
A type of antivirus software
A government cybersecurity initiative
questions.explanation:
Typosquatting exploits common typing mistakes by registering deceptive, similar-looking domains to trick users into
visiting fake sites.

questions.question: What is an "evil twin" Wi-Fi network?
options: A legitimate backup network provided by your ISP
A fake hotspot with a name nearly identical to a genuine one, created to intercept data
A type of antivirus feature
A network that only works with government devices
questions.explanation: Evil twin networks mimic a genuine Wi-Fi name to trick users into connecting, allowing attackers to intercept their data.

questions.question: What is "session hijacking"?
options: Ending your own browsing session safely
An attacker stealing your active login session to access an account without needing your password
A method of speeding up internet connections
A type of parental control feature
questions.explanation:
Session hijacking lets an attacker take over an already-authenticated session, bypassing the need to know your actual
password.

questions.question: How many devices does Google Safe Browsing reportedly protect daily?
options: About 1,000
Over 5 billion
About 500
About 10 million
questions.explanation:
Google Safe Browsing protects over 5 billion devices daily by checking websites and downloads against a constantly
updated threat list.

questions.question: What does Chrome's "Enhanced Protection" mode primarily add compared to standard protection?
options: It removes all browser security features
It uses AI to proactively detect new phishing and scam sites in real time
It disables all downloads permanently
It has no functional difference from standard protection
questions.explanation:
Enhanced Protection goes beyond a static list of known threats, using real-time AI analysis to catch newly emerging
phishing and scam sites.

questions.question:
Approximately how much safer from phishing/scams is Chrome's Enhanced Protection compared to Standard
Protection?
options: About 2 times safer
About 100 times safer
There is no measurable difference
It is actually less safe
questions.explanation:
Enhanced Protection is estimated to make users roughly twice as safe from phishing and scam websites compared to
Standard Protection.

questions.question: What does incognito/private browsing mode actually protect you from?
options: It makes you completely anonymous online
It only prevents your browsing history from being saved locally on your device
It protects you from phishing and malware entirely
It encrypts all your internet traffic
questions.explanation:
Incognito mode only avoids saving local browsing history; it does not hide your activity from websites or protect against
phishing/malware.

questions.question: What is a "VPN" (Virtual Private Network)?
options: A type of malware
A tool that encrypts your internet traffic for added privacy and security
A government surveillance program
A social media platform
questions.explanation:
A VPN encrypts your internet traffic, which can significantly reduce (though not eliminate) risk when using less secure
networks like public Wi-Fi.

questions.question: In a web address like "https://www.examplebank.com/login", what is the "domain"?
options: https://
www.
examplebank.com
/login✅ Correct Answer: Option C
questions.explanation:
The domain — here, examplebank.com — is the core identifying part of a website's address that confirms its actual
ownership.

questions.question: Why should you avoid downloading pirated or cracked versions of paid software?
options: Pirated software is always completely safe
Installing it often requires bypassing security checks, making it a common malware vector
There is no risk involved at all
Pirated software always performs better
questions.explanation:
Cracked software frequently requires disabling normal security protections, which criminals exploit to distribute malware
disguised as free paid software.

questions.question: What should you do if your browser warns that a file is "not commonly downloaded" and could be harmful?
options: Ignore the warning and download it anyway
Verify the source independently before proceeding
Disable browser warnings permanently
Share the file with friends immediately
questions.explanation:
Such warnings are based on real threat signals; verifying the file's source independently is the safer response than
dismissing the alert.

questions.question: Which of these best represents a fake government portal scam pattern?
options: A website exactly matching the official domain, offering free services
A look-alike site mimicking a government portal, charging unnecessary "service fees"
An official government website with no fees at all
A website requiring no personal information whatsoever
questions.explanation:
Fraudulent look-alike government portals commonly charge unnecessary fees for services that are free on the genuine
official site.

questions.question: What is the safest way to reach an official government service website?
options: Click a link shared in an unsolicited message
Search for and navigate directly to the officially known domain
Trust any link with "gov" somewhere in the URL
Use the first search result regardless of the domain
questions.explanation: Navigating directly to the confirmed official domain avoids the risk of clicking a fraudulent look-alike link.

questions.question: Why are unrealistic discounts on shopping websites considered a red flag?
options: Genuine retailers never offer discounts
Extremely steep discounts are a common tactic used by fake shopping websites to lure victims
Discounts always indicate a completely safe website
There is no connection between discounts and website legitimacy
questions.explanation:
Fake shopping sites often use unrealistically large discounts specifically to attract victims who then never receive their
purchased goods.

questions.question: What is the safest practice regarding Wi-Fi auto-connect settings?
options: Always enable auto-connect for convenience
Disable auto-connect, since attacker-controlled networks can sometimes mimic saved network names
Auto-connect settings have no security implications
Only enable auto-connect for public networks
questions.explanation:
Disabling auto-connect reduces the risk of your device automatically joining a malicious network disguised with a familiar
name.

questions.question: Which of these should you avoid doing on public Wi-Fi?
options: Reading general news articles
Conducting banking or UPI transactions without a VPN
Checking public weather updates
Browsing publicly available information
questions.explanation:
Sensitive transactions like banking or UPI payments carry higher risk on unsecured public Wi-Fi and should be avoided or
done via a trusted VPN.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of "malware injection" via public Wi-Fi?
options: A legitimate software update process
A compromised network pushing malicious pop-ups or redirecting downloads to install malware
A method banks use to verify transactions
A feature that improves Wi-Fi speed
questions.explanation:
Malware injection occurs when a compromised or malicious network is used to silently push harmful software onto
connected devices.

questions.question: What is the recommended action after finishing sensitive work on a public Wi-Fi network?
options: Leave the connection active indefinitely
Forget the network on your device once you're done using it
Share the Wi-Fi password with others nearby
Enable auto-connect for that specific network going forward
questions.explanation:
Forgetting the network afterward prevents your device from automatically reconnecting to it, or a similarly named
malicious network, in the future.

questions.question: Which of these is the safest source for downloading a browser extension?
options: A random third-party website offering "free premium extensions"
The browser's official extension store, after reviewing the requested permissions
A link shared via an unsolicited email
An unofficial forum post
questions.explanation:
Official extension stores provide some level of review, and checking permissions helps you avoid extensions that could
read everything you type or view.

questions.question:
Why is checking the "subdomain" of a website (like "www.") less useful for verifying authenticity compared to checking
the domain?
options: Subdomains are always more secure than domains
Subdomains are easily added or altered by anyone, unlike the core domain which identifies true ownership
Subdomains never appear in fake websites
There is no difference between them
questions.explanation:
While the domain reliably identifies the actual owner, subdomains can be freely created, making them a less reliable
authenticity signal.

questions.question: Approximately how many public Wi-Fi hotspots were estimated to be deployed globally, according to recent figures?
options: About 1,000
Approximately 950 million
About 50
About 100,000
questions.explanation:
The scale of nearly 950 million global public Wi-Fi hotspots highlights just how common — and therefore important to
secure — this connection method is.

questions.question: What should you check before entering payment details on any e-commerce website?
options: Only the visual design of the website
The exact domain spelling and HTTPS as a baseline, alongside overall legitimacy
Whether the website has a large number of pop-up ads
Nothing; all e-commerce sites are automatically safe
questions.explanation:
Careful domain verification combined with HTTPS as a minimum baseline helps confirm you're on a genuine site before
entering payment information.

questions.question: What is the primary risk of an "evil twin" network at an airport?
options: It slows down your internet speed only
It can intercept your data by tricking you into connecting to a fake hotspot resembling the genuine airport Wi-Fi
It automatically improves your device's battery life
It has no real security risk
questions.explanation:
Evil twin networks at high-traffic locations like airports specifically exploit travellers' need for convenient Wi-Fi to intercept
their data.

questions.question: Why might free VPN services sometimes be less trustworthy than paid, reputable ones?
options: Free VPNs are always more secure
Some free VPNs have weaker security or may log and sell user data themselves
There is no difference in trustworthiness between free and paid VPNs
Free VPNs are illegal in all countries
questions.explanation:
Some free VPN providers monetise by logging and selling user data, which can undermine the very privacy protection
users are seeking.

questions.question: What is the safest response if two nearly identically named free Wi-Fi networks are available at a public venue?
options: Connect to whichever one has a stronger signal
Verify with venue staff which network is genuine before connecting to either
Connect to both simultaneously for redundancy
Assume both are equally safe and pick randomly
questions.explanation:
Verifying with staff helps avoid connecting to a fraudulent evil-twin network set up specifically to mimic the venue's real
Wi-Fi.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects safe file-download practice?
options: Download files only from official, verified sources
Download any file regardless of source if it looks interesting
Ignore file extensions entirely when downloading
Assume all downloads are automatically safe
questions.explanation:
Sticking to official, verified download sources significantly reduces the risk of installing malware disguised as a legitimate
file.

questions.question: What is a reasonable response to an unexpected .exe file attached to an email from an unfamiliar sender?
options: Open it immediately out of curiosity
Treat it with strong suspicion and avoid opening it without independent verification
Forward it to colleagues to open first
Rename the file extension to make it safe
questions.explanation:
Unexpected executable files from unfamiliar senders are a common malware delivery method and should be treated with
significant caution.

questions.question: What is the primary function of Google Safe Browsing?
options: To speed up website loading times
To check websites and downloads against a constantly updated list of known dangerous sites
To block all advertisements on every website
To manage your saved passwords
questions.explanation:
Google Safe Browsing works in the background across major browsers, flagging known malicious sites and downloads to
protect users.

questions.question: Which of these situations illustrates a "look-alike government portal" scam?
options: The official passport portal charging its standard, published fee
A fraudulent site mimicking the passport portal, charging an extra unofficial "processing fee"
A citizen visiting the correct official domain directly
A government office providing free in-person assistance
questions.explanation: Fake look-alike government sites commonly add unnecessary, unofficial fees that the genuine portal doesn't charge.

questions.question: What does it mean if your password manager fails to auto-fill your credentials on a website you're visiting?
options: It always indicates a technical glitch with no security relevance
It could be a useful signal that you may be on a fake, look-alike domain rather than the genuine site
It means your password has expired
It means the website has no login page
questions.explanation:
Since password managers only auto-fill on the exact saved domain, a failure to do so can help you notice you might be on
a fraudulent site.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the recommended balance between convenience and safety for public Wi-Fi use?
options: Avoid public Wi-Fi for any purpose whatsoever
Use public Wi-Fi for non-sensitive activities, but avoid or use a VPN for sensitive tasks like banking
Use public Wi-Fi for all banking without any precautions
Public Wi-Fi carries no meaningful risk difference from home networks
questions.explanation:
A balanced approach allows convenient use of public Wi-Fi for low-risk activities while reserving extra caution (or a VPN)
for sensitive tasks.

questions.question:
What is the risk of clicking a link in an SMS claiming your "bank account will be suspended" unless you verify
immediately?
options: There is no risk if the message looks official
It may lead to a phishing site designed to steal your banking credentials
It is always a genuine, safe verification process
It automatically improves your account's security
questions.explanation:
Such urgent SMS messages are a common smishing tactic; clicking the link risks landing on a fraudulent site designed to
harvest your credentials.

questions.question: Which of these best describes the purpose of checking a website's domain "character by character"?
options: It has no real value in verifying authenticity
It helps catch subtle misspellings, extra words, or hyphens used in fraudulent look-alike domains
It is only relevant for extremely long domain names
It only matters for banking websites, not others
questions.explanation:
Fraudulent domains often differ from genuine ones by only a letter or an added word, making careful, character-by-
character checking valuable.

questions.question: What should you do if you're unsure whether a browser extension is safe before installing it?
options: Install it immediately regardless of source
Review its requested permissions and only install from the official browser extension store
Assume all extensions are automatically safe
Install it only on someone else's device to test it
questions.explanation:
Checking requested permissions and sourcing extensions only from the official store helps avoid malicious extensions that
could capture your data.

questions.question: Approximately how many suspicious files does Chrome's Enhanced Protection reportedly scan monthly?
options: About 10
About 50
questions.explanation:
Chrome's Enhanced Protection scans a significant volume of suspicious files monthly, reflecting the scale of proactive
threat detection it provides.

questions.question: Why is "HTTPS" alone insufficient to fully trust a website?
options: HTTPS guarantees the website's content is accurate and genuine
HTTPS only confirms encryption of the connection, not the legitimacy of the site's owner
HTTPS is only used by government websites
HTTPS makes a website immune to phishing
questions.explanation:
HTTPS protects the data in transit through encryption but says nothing about whether the website itself is operated by a
legitimate, trustworthy entity.

questions.question:
What is the safest approach to a message offering an unbelievably high "cashback" for scanning a QR code or visiting a
link?
options: Act immediately to claim the reward before it expires
Treat it with scepticism and verify independently, since unrealistic offers are a common scam pattern
Share the offer widely without verification
Assume it's genuine since it references a real bank's name
questions.explanation: Unrealistic reward offers are a widely used tactic to lure victims into scams; independent verification is the safe response.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why security researchers observe spikes in fake websites around festive shopping seasons?
options: Fake websites only appear during non-shopping periods
Increased shopping activity creates more opportunities for scammers to exploit consumer urgency and demand
There is no seasonal pattern to fake website activity
Genuine retailers create most of the fake websites themselves
questions.explanation:
High shopping activity during festive seasons creates fertile ground for scammers to exploit urgency and demand with
fraudulent shopping sites.

questions.question: What is the primary reason banking transactions are discouraged on public Wi-Fi without protection?
options: Public Wi-Fi always has slower speeds, which is the only concern
Unsecured public networks make it easier for attackers to intercept sensitive data in transit
Banks legally prohibit any use of public Wi-Fi
There is no real risk difference from private networks
questions.explanation:
Because public Wi-Fi is often less secure, sensitive data like banking credentials can potentially be intercepted by
attackers on the same network.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a responsible way to handle privacy on a shared/public computer?
options: Save your passwords for convenience
Use private/incognito mode if available and always log out fully afterward
Leave your accounts logged in for the next user
Avoid clearing any browsing data afterward
questions.explanation:
Using private browsing and logging out completely helps ensure the next user of a shared device cannot access your
accounts or data.

questions.question: What does it mean if a website asks for information far beyond what seems necessary for its stated purpose?
options: This is completely normal and expected behaviour
It may be a red flag suggesting the site could be attempting to over-collect or misuse personal data
It always indicates strong security practices
It has no bearing on the site's trustworthiness
questions.explanation:
Requests for excessive or irrelevant personal information can indicate a site attempting to collect more data than
legitimately needed, which is worth scrutinising.

questions.question:
Why do experts recommend verifying an organisation's official website independently rather than clicking a provided
link?
options: Clicking provided links is always completely safe
Provided links, especially in unsolicited messages, can lead to fraudulent look-alike sites instead of the genuine one
Independent verification is unnecessary and outdated advice
Organisations never provide direct links to their own websites
questions.explanation:
Independently navigating to a known, official website avoids the risk of a provided link secretly redirecting to a fraudulent
look-alike page.

questions.question: What is the relationship between "browser extensions" and data privacy risk?
options: Extensions have no access to any of your browsing data
A malicious extension can potentially read everything you type or view within your browser
Extensions are always vetted perfectly with zero risk
Extensions cannot be installed without government approval
questions.explanation:
Because extensions can have deep access to browser activity, a malicious one poses a significant privacy and security risk if
installed carelessly.

questions.question:
What is the safest response to a browser notification claiming "You've won a prize, claim now" while browsing a random
website?
options: Click through immediately to claim the prize
Treat it as a likely scam or malicious ad and avoid interacting with it
Enter your personal details to verify eligibility
Share the notification with friends to claim together
questions.explanation:
Unsolicited "prize" notifications are a common malicious advertising or phishing tactic and should be avoided rather than
engaged with.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why checking a website's domain matters more than judging its visual design?
options: Visual design is always a reliable indicator of legitimacy
Fraudulent websites can closely copy a genuine site's design, but they cannot replicate the actual registered domain
Domains are irrelevant to website authenticity
Visual design and domain checking are equally unreliable
questions.explanation:
While scammers can copy a website's appearance convincingly, they cannot use the exact same registered domain as the
genuine site, making domain-checking more reliable.

questions.question: What is the recommended habit regarding Wi-Fi networks you no longer use or trust?
options: Keep all previously connected networks saved indefinitely
Remove/forget networks you no longer use or trust from your device's saved list
Share your saved network list with others
There is no security reason to manage saved networks
questions.explanation:
Removing outdated or untrusted saved networks reduces the chance of your device automatically reconnecting to a
potentially compromised network.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the core relationship between "convenience" and "safety" when using public Wi-Fi and
downloads?
options: Convenience should always be prioritised over any safety consideration

A few extra verification steps (checking domains, avoiding sensitive tasks on public Wi-Fi) meaningfully reduce risk
without eliminating convenience entirely
Safety and convenience can never coexist in any way
There is no trade-off to consider at all
questions.explanation:
Small, consistent verification habits allow you to retain much of the convenience of public Wi-Fi and downloads while
significantly reducing associated risks.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the most effective overall habit for safe internet usage?
options: Trusting any website that loads without an error message
Verifying the network, the source, and the domain every single time before trusting or entering sensitive information
Avoiding the internet entirely to eliminate all risk
Relying solely on your device's default settings with no active verification
questions.explanation:
Consistently verifying networks, download sources, and domains before trusting them is the central habit that prevents
the vast majority of safe-internet-usage risks.

questions.question: What is the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal's web address?
options: cybercrime.gov.in
cybersafety.com
reportfraud.org
safeindia.net✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation: cybercrime.gov.in is India's official portal for reporting all categories of cybercrime, run under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.question: What is the toll-free number for reporting financial cyber fraud in India?
options: 181✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: 1930 is India's dedicated 24x7 helpline specifically for reporting financial cyber fraud quickly.

questions.question: What is meant by the "golden hour" in cybercrime reporting?
options: The best time of day to use the internet
The first hour after discovering fraud, offering the best chance of freezing stolen funds
A one-hour customer service window
The hour banks are closed for maintenance
questions.explanation:
The golden hour refers to the critical early window when banks and NCRP's tracing system have the best chance of
freezing stolen money before it disappears.

questions.question: Is filing a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in the same as filing an FIR?
options: Yes, they are identical in every respect
No, a portal complaint is an acknowledged report, but serious cases may still require a formal FIR
FIRs are always filed automatically after any portal complaint
Portal complaints have no legal standing whatsoever
questions.explanation:
A portal complaint is acknowledged and tracked, but it isn't automatically the same as a formal FIR, which may still be
needed for serious cases.

questions.question: What is a "Zero FIR"?
options: An FIR that cannot be registered anywhere
An FIR that can be registered at any police station, regardless of jurisdiction, and later transferred
An FIR requiring zero evidence
An FIR that expires after zero days
questions.explanation:
A Zero FIR allows a crime to be reported at any police station, which is then transferred to the appropriate jurisdiction for
investigation.

questions.question: What is the "e-Zero FIR" initiative, introduced by I4C in May 2025?
options: A scheme unrelated to cybercrime
A mechanism automatically registering a Zero FIR for financial-fraud complaints above ₹10 lakh made via NCRP/1930
A requirement that all complaints must be filed in person
A rule eliminating the need to report any fraud at all
questions.explanation:
The e-Zero FIR mechanism speeds up formal investigation for high-value fraud complaints by automatically triggering FIR
registration above a set threshold.

questions.question: What is CFCFRMS?
options: A social media platform
The Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System, used to trace and freeze stolen funds
A type of antivirus software
A government tax portal
questions.explanation:
CFCFRMS is the backend system used by banks, police, and payment providers to trace and freeze funds after a financial
fraud complaint.

questions.question: What evidence should you collect immediately after a suspected cyber fraud?
options: Nothing; evidence collection is unnecessary
Screenshots with visible timestamps, transaction IDs, and any relevant URLs
Only your own memory of what happened
A verbal account shared only with friends
questions.explanation:
Screenshots with timestamps, transaction IDs, and URLs provide concrete evidence that strengthens your complaint and
supports investigation.

questions.question: Should you delete or edit messages related to a fraud before reporting it?
options: Yes, always delete them immediately
No, you should preserve the original messages/evidence exactly as received
Editing them to be more concise is recommended
It doesn't matter either way
questions.explanation:
Preserving original evidence without editing or deleting ensures it remains valid and useful for investigation and any
formal proceedings.

questions.question:
Within how many working days should you report an unauthorised bank transaction to potentially benefit from zero
liability?
options: 30 days
3 working days
1 year
6 months✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
RBI's rules provide zero customer liability if unauthorised transactions are reported within 3 working days, provided the
fault isn't the customer's own.

questions.question: Which portal should you use to report a lost or stolen mobile phone in India?
options: cybercrime.gov.in only
Sanchar Saathi (sancharsaathi.gov.in)
UMANG exclusively
MyGov✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: Sanchar Saathi lets you block and trace a lost or stolen phone using its IMEI number through the CEIR system.

questions.question: Where should you file a complaint about a personal data breach by a company or app?
options: The local police station only
The Data Protection Board of India, under the DPDP Act
The Election Commission of India
The Ministry of Railways
questions.explanation:
The Data Protection Board of India is the designated authority for handling complaints related to personal data breaches
under the DPDP Act, 2023.

questions.question: Which category on cybercrime.gov.in should be used for crimes against women or children?
options: "Report Other Cyber Crime"
"Report Women/Child Related Crime"
There is no specific category for this
"General Feedback"
questions.explanation:
The portal has a dedicated category specifically for crimes against women and children, ensuring these sensitive cases are
handled appropriately.

questions.question: What acknowledgement do you receive after successfully filing a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in?
options: Nothing at all
A 14-digit acknowledgement number sent via SMS
A physical letter mailed within a year
An automatic bank refund
questions.explanation: A 14-digit acknowledgement number, starting with "2" and sent via SMS, allows you to track your complaint's progress.

questions.question: How much did reported cyber fraud losses in India total in 2024?
options: About ₹100 crore
Approximately ₹22,845 crore
About ₹5 crore
About ₹1 lakh crore
questions.explanation:
Reported cyber fraud losses reached approximately ₹22,845 crore in 2024, reflecting the scale of financial cybercrime in
India.

questions.question: Between April 2021 and September 2025, what percentage of the total defrauded amount was reportedly recovered?
options: About 90%
About 6.7%
About 50%
100%✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
Only around 6.7% of the roughly ₹3,588 crore defrauded amount was recovered in this period, underscoring why speed in
reporting matters so much.

questions.question: Which agency coordinates India's national cybercrime response and administers the NCRP portal?
options: UIDAI
Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)
SEBI
Ministry of Railways
questions.explanation:
I4C, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, coordinates the national cybercrime reporting infrastructure, including NCRP and
the 1930 helpline.

questions.question: Where should you report investment or stockbroker-related fraud?
options: Sanchar Saathi
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Election Commission of India
Ministry of Railways
questions.explanation: SEBI's official complaint channels are the appropriate route for reporting fraud related to investments or stockbrokers.

questions.question: What should you do if your bank doesn't resolve a complaint satisfactorily?
options: Give up entirely, since nothing more can be done
Escalate to RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme
Post about it on social media instead of any formal channel
Close all your accounts immediately
questions.explanation: The RBI Ombudsman Scheme provides a formal, free escalation path for unresolved banking service complaints.

questions.question: Which of these best describes the increase in cybercrime incidents in India from 2022 to 2024?
options: Incidents decreased significantly
Incidents rose from about 10.29 lakh to about 22.68 lakh, roughly a 120% increase
There was no meaningful change
Incidents increased by only 5%
questions.explanation:
This dramatic rise highlights the growing scale of cybercrime in India and the corresponding importance of knowing how
to report it effectively.

questions.question:
Priya notices a fraudulent ₹15,000 UPI debit just minutes ago. What is the recommended immediate sequence of
actions?
options: Wait a week to see if the bank notices on its own
Call 1930 immediately, then her bank, then file a detailed complaint on cybercrime.gov.in the same day
Only post about it on social media
Change her social media password only
questions.explanation:
Acting within the golden hour by calling 1930 and the bank immediately, followed by a detailed portal complaint,
maximises the chance of fund recovery.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of an "FIR" (First Information Report)?
options: A casual complaint with no legal standing
The formal police document that begins a criminal investigation
A type of bank statement
A government tax form
questions.explanation: An FIR is the official document that formally initiates a police investigation into a reported crime.

questions.question: Which of these accurately reflects jurisdiction rules for filing a cybercrime complaint in India?
options: You can only file at the police station exactly where the crime occurred
Cybercrime has nationwide jurisdiction, allowing complaints to be filed at any cyber crime cell
Cybercrime complaints can never be filed at a police station
Only complaints above ₹1 crore can be filed anywhere
questions.explanation:
Because cybercrime often crosses geographic boundaries, complaints can be registered at any cyber crime cell, regardless
of where the crime occurred.

questions.question: What should family members do to help a relative who is a victim of cybercrime?
options: Avoid getting involved under any circumstances
Help preserve evidence and support making the initial report as quickly as possible
Wait for the victim to handle everything entirely alone
Discourage the victim from reporting to avoid embarrassment
questions.explanation:
Supporting quick evidence preservation and reporting can make a meaningful difference in the chances of resolving or
recovering from cyber fraud.

questions.question:
What is the national emergency number relevant for any immediate danger, including some cyber-related
emergencies?
options: 181✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
112 is India's unified emergency number for immediate danger situations, complementing specialised helplines like 1930
for financial cyber fraud.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT typically required as evidence when reporting cyber fraud?
options: Screenshots with timestamps
Transaction IDs
The suspect's exact home address, which is often unknown
Any available suspect contact details, like a phone number or UPI ID
questions.explanation:
While useful if known, a suspect's exact home address is rarely available to victims; other digital evidence is what's typically
collected and reported.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to back up evidence to a separate device or cloud storage?
options: Backing up evidence has no practical benefit
In case your original device is later needed for forensic examination or becomes inaccessible
To make the evidence harder to find later
Only businesses need to back up evidence, not individuals
questions.explanation:
A separate backup ensures evidence remains accessible even if your original device is examined, lost, or otherwise
unavailable later.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct process order for filing an NCRP complaint?
options: Submit first, then register with mobile/email verification afterward

Register with mobile and email (OTP verified), choose the category, fill details, submit, and note the acknowledgement
number
There is no structured process; complaints are informal
Registration is not required at all
questions.explanation:
This is the standard NCRP process, ensuring your complaint is properly registered, categorised, and trackable via an
acknowledgement number.

questions.question:
What is the correct response to a family member being harassed online with threats and non-consensual image
sharing?
options: Handle it informally without any reporting
Treat it seriously, preserve evidence, and report via cybercrime.gov.in or relevant helplines like 1098/181
Ignore it since online threats are rarely serious
Confront the harasser directly without any documentation
questions.explanation:
Serious threats or non-consensual image sharing require formal reporting through appropriate channels, backed by
preserved evidence.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why "speed" matters so much in cybercrime reporting?
options: Speed has no real impact on the outcome
Stolen funds move quickly through multiple accounts, so delayed reporting sharply reduces recovery chances
Reporting quickly guarantees a full refund in all cases
Reporting speed only matters for non-financial crimes
questions.explanation:
Because fraudulent funds are moved rapidly across accounts, reporting within the golden hour significantly increases the
chance of a successful freeze.

questions.question: What number specifically serves as CHILDLINE, India's child helpline?
options: 112✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: 1098 is CHILDLINE, India's 24x7 helpline dedicated to helping children in distress or in need of protection.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct definition of the "Women's Helpline"?
options: 100✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: 181 is a dedicated women's helpline addressing harassment, safety concerns, and related issues.

questions.question: What happens if you file a portal complaint for a serious, high-value cybercrime?
options: No further action is ever needed beyond the portal complaint
You may still need to visit a Cyber Crime Police Station to register a formal FIR within the prescribed timeframe
The complaint automatically becomes invalid after filing
Portal complaints for serious crimes are not permitted at all
questions.explanation:
While the portal registers your complaint, serious or high-value cases may still require escalating to a formal FIR at a police
station.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct definition of "financial loss recovery" challenges in cybercrime?
options: Recovery is always guaranteed regardless of reporting speed
Recovery rates have historically been low, making prompt reporting within the golden hour especially critical
Recovery has nothing to do with how quickly a crime is reported
Recovery is only possible for losses above ₹1 crore
questions.explanation:
Given the historically low overall recovery rate, acting quickly within the golden hour offers the best realistic chance of
recovering stolen funds.

questions.question: What should a victim do if uncertain about which NCRP category applies to their specific situation?
options: Avoid filing any complaint at all
Choose the closest matching category and provide clear details, since categories help route the complaint appropriately
File the complaint anonymously with no details
Wait until the situation resolves itself
questions.explanation:
Choosing the closest matching category with clear details helps ensure the complaint is routed to the right authorities for
handling.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why reporting cybercrime "no matter how small the amount" is still worthwhile?
options: Small losses have zero investigative value
All reports, regardless of amount, contribute to broader investigations and pattern detection
Only losses above ₹10 lakh should ever be reported
Small-amount frauds are not covered by any reporting system
questions.explanation:
Every reported cybercrime, regardless of size, adds to the data that helps authorities detect patterns and pursue broader
investigations.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of "I4C"?
options: A private cybersecurity company
The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, under the Ministry of Home Affairs
An international banking regulator
A social media platform
questions.explanation:
I4C coordinates India's national cybercrime response, including the NCRP portal, 1930 helpline, and initiatives like the e-
Zero FIR mechanism.

questions.question: Which of these best describes what happens when you report a lost phone via Sanchar Saathi?
options: Nothing happens; the portal only provides information
Your device can be blocked and traced using its IMEI number
The portal automatically files a police FIR without any input
Sanchar Saathi only works for phones purchased outside India
questions.explanation:
Sanchar Saathi's CEIR system allows you to block and trace a lost or stolen device based on its IMEI, helping prevent
misuse.

questions.question: What is the correct action if you receive threatening messages from an anonymous account targeting your teenager?
options: Delete the messages immediately without any other action
Preserve the messages, and file a complaint under "Report Women/Child Related Crime" or call 1098
Ignore it since teenagers often exaggerate online conflicts
Confront the anonymous account directly without documentation
questions.explanation:
Preserving evidence and using the appropriate reporting channel ensures the matter is handled seriously and through
the correct process.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the purpose of tracking your NCRP complaint status through your portal dashboard?
options: Tracking has no practical value once a complaint is filed
It lets you monitor progress and follow up if the matter remains unresolved
Tracking is only available for complaints above ₹50 lakh
Only police officers can view complaint status, never the complainant
questions.explanation:
Regularly checking your complaint's status helps you stay informed and follow up proactively rather than passively waiting
for resolution.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of "zero liability" under RBI's rules for unauthorised electronic transactions?
options: Customers are always liable for 100% of any loss

Customers may bear no liability for unauthorised transactions if reported within the required timeframe and not due to
their own negligence
Zero liability applies only to cash withdrawals
Zero liability has no connection to reporting timelines
questions.explanation:
RBI's rules protect customers from liability for unauthorised transactions when reported promptly and when the customer
wasn't at fault.

questions.question:
Which of these situations would most appropriately be reported through the "Report Other Cyber Crime" category on
NCRP?
options: A fake website scam unrelated to women/child safety
A missing person report
A property tax dispute
A traffic violation
questions.explanation:
General cybercrime issues like fake website scams fall under the "Report Other Cyber Crime" category, distinct from the
dedicated women/child crime category.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to ensure your cybercrime complaint isn't lost or forgotten?
options: Rely entirely on memory without any written record
Note and safely store your acknowledgement/complaint number for future reference and tracking
Assume the authorities will contact you without needing any reference
File the same complaint repeatedly without any tracking number
questions.explanation:
Keeping your acknowledgement number safe allows you to reliably track, follow up, and reference your complaint
whenever needed.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate action if evidence involves a dynamic, disappearing message (like a Story)?
options: Ignore it since it can't be captured
Use a screen recording to capture it before it disappears
Wait for it to reappear naturally
Ask the sender to resend it later
questions.explanation:
Screen recording captures dynamic or temporary content, like Stories or live streams, before it becomes permanently
unavailable.

questions.question: What is the correct relationship between "CFCFRMS" and financial fraud complaints?
options: CFCFRMS has no connection to financial fraud reporting
It is used specifically to trace and freeze fraudulently transferred funds after a financial-fraud complaint is filed
CFCFRMS only applies to non-financial crimes
CFCFRMS replaces the need to ever contact your bank
questions.explanation:
CFCFRMS is the specific system enabling banks and police to trace and freeze funds following a reported financial cyber
fraud.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a mistake commonly made by cybercrime victims?
options: Reporting the incident within the first hour
Waiting several days before reporting, losing the advantage of the golden hour
Preserving evidence before blocking a suspicious contact
Noting the complaint acknowledgement number
questions.explanation:
Delaying reporting significantly reduces the chance of recovering stolen funds, making prompt action one of the most
important habits to maintain.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of the "Data Protection Board of India"?
options: A private company offering data backup services
The regulator handling complaints related to personal data breaches under the DPDP Act, 2023
A department managing India's railway data
An international human rights body
questions.explanation:
The Data Protection Board of India specifically handles grievances and enforcement related to personal data protection
violations.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct approach when uncertain whether an incident constitutes a "portal complaint"
matter or requires a formal FIR?
options: Assume portal complaints are always sufficient for every situation
File the portal complaint first, and escalate to a formal FIR at a police station if the situation is serious or unresolved
Skip the portal entirely and go straight to court
Avoid any reporting until absolutely certain of the correct process
questions.explanation:
Starting with a portal complaint while remaining open to escalating to a formal FIR ensures the issue is addressed
through the appropriate, complete process.

questions.question: Which of these accurately reflects the scale of the 1930 helpline and NCRP system's importance in India?
options: They handle only a handful of complaints each year

They form a critical part of India's response to a cybercrime landscape involving millions of incidents and significant
financial losses annually
They are rarely used by the general public
They exist only in a few select cities
questions.explanation:
Given the scale of cybercrime incidents and losses reported annually in India, the 1930 helpline and NCRP portal play a
critical nationwide role.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the single most important overall lesson about reporting cyber crime?
options: Reporting is optional and rarely makes a difference

Acting quickly, using the correct channel, and preserving evidence together offer the best chance of resolution and
recovery
Only large financial losses are worth the effort of reporting
Evidence collection is unnecessary if you report quickly enough
questions.explanation:
Speed, correct reporting channels, and careful evidence preservation work together as the three pillars of effective
cybercrime reporting and recovery.

questions.question: What does "cyber hygiene" mean?
options: A one-time security setup that never needs revisiting
Routine, repeated safety habits that keep devices and accounts secure over time
A government tax on internet usage
A type of antivirus subscription
questions.explanation: Cyber hygiene refers to consistent, repeated habits — not a single setup — similar to ongoing personal hygiene practices.

questions.question: What is "Cyber Jaagrookta Diwas"?
options: An annual government holiday
India's monthly cybersecurity awareness observance, held on the first Wednesday of every month since May 2022
A one-time cybersecurity conference
A private company's marketing campaign
questions.explanation:
Cyber Jaagrookta Diwas is a recurring, monthly observance mandated by the Ministry of Home Affairs to reinforce
cybersecurity awareness regularly.

questions.question: When is India's National Cyber Security Awareness Month observed?
options: Every January
Every October
Every June
It is not observed annually
questions.explanation:
National Cyber Security Awareness Month is observed every October, led by CERT-In and MeitY, featuring themed
campaigns and citizen resources.

questions.question: Which of these is classified as a "daily" cyber safety habit?
options: Auditing all app permissions in depth
Never sharing an OTP, password, or PIN with anyone
Reviewing privacy settings on social media
Checking Aadhaar Authentication History
questions.explanation:
Never sharing OTPs or passwords is a habit that applies every single day, across nearly every digital interaction, making it a
"daily" priority.

questions.question: Which of these is best classified as a "weekly" cyber safety habit?
options: Locking your device screen when stepping away
Reviewing your bank and UPI transaction history for anything unfamiliar
Removing unused apps and dormant accounts
Updating weak or reused passwords
questions.explanation:
A weekly transaction review strikes a good balance — frequent enough to catch problems early, without requiring daily
deep review.

questions.question: Which of these is best classified as a "monthly" cyber safety habit?
options: Verifying a UPI payee name before confirming
Auditing and revoking unnecessary app permissions
Disconnecting from a suspicious call
Locking your screen
questions.explanation:
A deeper review like auditing app permissions doesn't need to happen daily or weekly, making a monthly cadence
appropriate.

questions.question: Which of these is an "as-needed" (emergency) cyber safety action?
options: Reviewing privacy settings once a month
Calling 1930 and your bank immediately upon suspecting financial fraud
Checking for software updates weekly
Locking your device screen daily
questions.explanation:
Emergency actions like calling 1930 immediately are triggered only when an actual incident occurs, not on a fixed
schedule.

questions.question: What is the recommended response to a "digital arrest" or urgent threat call, according to the as-needed checklist?
options: Stay on the call to gather more information
Disconnect immediately
Negotiate calmly with the caller
Ask a family member to join the call first
questions.explanation:
Disconnecting immediately is the correct as-needed response, since no genuine authority conducts arrests or
investigations over a call.

questions.question:
Which cadence category does "checking for and installing pending software updates" fall under, according to the
checklist framework?
options: Daily
Weekly
Never
Only once, at initial device setup
questions.explanation:
Checking for updates weekly strikes a practical balance, ensuring patches are applied promptly without requiring daily
manual checks.

questions.question:
What is the primary reason the government promotes cybersecurity awareness on a recurring monthly and annual
basis, rather than as a single campaign?
options: Recurring awareness has no added benefit over a single session
Awareness fades over time without repetition, so ongoing reinforcement is more effective
Monthly campaigns are required only for government employees
A single campaign is always sufficient for lasting behaviour change
questions.explanation:
Just as this module argues, awareness needs repetition to remain effective, which is why India observes both monthly and
annual cybersecurity campaigns.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "verifying the payee name before confirming a UPI payment" is placed in the daily
habits category?
options: It only needs to be done once per month
It's a quick, frequent action tied directly to an everyday activity — making payments
It has no real security value
It should only be done for large transactions
questions.explanation:
Since UPI payments happen frequently, verifying the payee name each time is naturally a daily-level habit, taking only
seconds per transaction.

questions.question: What is the recommended step if you discover you've never done a "monthly" privacy/permissions review before?
options: It's too late to start, so there's no point beginning now
Start this month, since a late start is still far better than never beginning
Only start once you've experienced a security incident
Only children should perform this type of review
questions.explanation: Starting the habit now, regardless of past neglect, still provides meaningful ongoing protection going forward.

questions.question: Which of these is recommended as part of your "as-needed" response to a lost or stolen phone?
options: Wait a few weeks before taking any action
Report it immediately via the Sanchar Saathi portal to block/trace the device
Ignore it if the phone was inexpensive
Only inform friends on social media
questions.explanation: Prompt reporting via Sanchar Saathi allows the device to be blocked or traced quickly, reducing the risk of misuse.

questions.question: What should trigger an "as-needed" report to the Data Protection Board of India?
options: A routine weekly review of your own privacy settings
Suspicion that a company or app has experienced a data breach involving your personal data
Updating your own password
Installing a new app
questions.explanation:
Suspected data breaches by companies handling your personal data are an as-needed trigger for a formal complaint to
the Data Protection Board.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the intended purpose of organising cyber safety habits into a "cadence framework" (daily/
weekly/monthly/as-needed)?
options: To make cyber safety feel more complicated and time-consuming
To make cyber safety sustainable by matching habit frequency to its actual importance and urgency
To ensure all habits are performed only once a year
To eliminate the need for any emergency response planning
questions.explanation:
Organising habits by cadence helps make cyber safety practical and sustainable, rather than overwhelming, by matching
frequency to real need.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a mistake related to treating cyber safety as a "set it once and forget it" task?
options: Reviewing app permissions periodically as habits change
Assuming a single initial security setup will remain sufficient indefinitely
Following a structured daily/weekly/monthly routine
Teaching family members ongoing safe habits
questions.explanation:
Cyber safety requires ongoing maintenance; assuming a one-time setup is sufficient overlooks how threats, settings, and
habits change over time.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why involving your whole family in a shared cyber safety routine is recommended?
options: Family involvement has no meaningful security benefit
It multiplies the protection of the routine, since awareness is only as strong as its weakest, least-informed member
Only adults need to understand these concepts
Family involvement should be limited strictly to financial matters
questions.explanation:
Since any family member can be targeted, involving the whole household ensures consistent awareness and reduces the
household's overall vulnerability.

questions.question: What is the recommended first 30-minute step when setting up a brand-new device?
options: Immediately install unfamiliar third-party apps
Enable a strong screen lock and turn on automatic software updates
Disable all built-in security features for faster performance
Skip any account setup indefinitely
questions.explanation:
Establishing a strong screen lock and automatic updates from the very start builds a secure foundation before any other
apps or accounts are added.

questions.question:
In the "first 30 minutes" device setup sequence, which account should typically be secured with Two-Factor
Authentication first?
options: A gaming account
Email, since it's often the recovery gateway to other accounts
A rarely used shopping account
A social media account created just for fun
questions.explanation:
Because password resets for many services route through email, securing email with 2FA first protects the gateway to your
broader digital identity.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the recommended "weekly 10-minute routine" concept?
options: A lengthy, multi-hour security audit performed weekly
A short, focused set of checks (transactions, updates, requests, new app permissions) completing in about 10 minutes
A routine that only applies to business accounts
An annual review disguised as a weekly one
questions.explanation:
The weekly routine is intentionally brief and focused, making it realistic to sustain consistently without feeling
burdensome.

questions.question:
Which of these habits specifically ties back to protecting your digital identity and privacy, as covered by the daily/
weekly/monthly framework?
options: Reviewing privacy settings and auditing app permissions monthly
Locking your device screen only once a year
Ignoring app permission requests entirely
Sharing your Aadhaar number publicly for convenience
questions.explanation:
Monthly privacy and permission reviews directly reinforce the digital identity and privacy protections covered earlier in this
category.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the checklist's guidance on checking your Aadhaar Authentication History?
options: It should be checked only once, at the time of Aadhaar enrolment
It is recommended as part of a monthly review to catch unfamiliar authentication activity
It has no relevance to ongoing cyber safety
It should be checked exclusively by banks, not individuals
questions.explanation:
Including this in the monthly review helps citizens proactively catch any unauthorised use of their Aadhaar for
authentication.

questions.question: What is the recommended response upon noticing an unfamiliar small UPI debit from a few days ago?
options: Ignore it since a few days have already passed
Report it via 1930 as soon as noticed, even if some time has passed
Wait until the end of the year to review it
Assume banks automatically catch and reverse all unfamiliar debits
questions.explanation:
Even after a short delay, reporting promptly once noticed is far better than continuing to wait, since recovery chances
decline further with more delay.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the intended relationship between this capstone module and the previous nine modules
in the category?
options: It introduces entirely new, unrelated topics
It consolidates and organises key habits from the previous nine modules into one practical, repeatable routine
It replaces the need to have learned the previous modules at all
It focuses solely on advanced technical hacking techniques
questions.explanation:
This module is explicitly designed as a synthesis, drawing together the most important habits from every earlier module
into one usable checklist.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate use of calendar reminders in maintaining cyber hygiene?
options: Calendar reminders are unnecessary and add no value
Setting a recurring monthly reminder helps ensure deeper reviews don't lapse over time
Reminders should only be set once, for a single one-time review
Reminders are relevant only for professional, not personal, cyber safety
questions.explanation:
A recurring reminder helps sustain the monthly review habit long-term, preventing it from being forgotten amid daily
busyness.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the checklist's guidance on removing unused apps, dormant wallets, or inactive accounts?
options: This should be done only once, immediately after buying a new phone
This is recommended as part of the monthly review to reduce overall exposure
Unused apps and accounts pose no security risk and can be left indefinitely
Only businesses need to worry about dormant accounts
questions.explanation:
Periodically removing unused apps and dormant accounts reduces the number of potential weak points that could be
exploited if compromised.

questions.question:
What is the recommended action for a workplace wanting to align internal cybersecurity awareness sessions with a
national observance?
options: Choose a random, unrelated date each year
Align sessions with the monthly Cyber Jaagrookta Diwas date used by many government-linked institutions
Avoid any formal alignment with national observances
Hold sessions only once, at company founding
questions.explanation:
Aligning with the established monthly Cyber Jaagrookta Diwas date provides a consistent, recognised cadence for
reinforcing awareness at work.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why the "as-needed" category doesn't have a fixed schedule, unlike daily/weekly/monthly
habits?
options: As-needed actions are actually scheduled annually
As-needed actions are triggered specifically by an actual incident occurring, not by the passage of time
As-needed actions should be performed constantly, regardless of circumstances
There is no real difference between as-needed and daily habits
questions.explanation:
Unlike routine habits tied to a calendar, as-needed actions respond directly to specific incidents as they arise, such as
suspected fraud or harassment.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the checklist's guidance regarding harassment or exploitation involving a minor?
options: Handle it informally without involving any authority
Preserve evidence, then report via cybercrime.gov.in, 1098, or 181 as appropriate
Wait to see if the situation resolves on its own
Confront the harasser directly without any documentation
questions.explanation:
Serious concerns involving minors require formal, evidence-backed reporting through the appropriate specialised
channels, consistent with earlier modules.

questions.question: Which of these best summarises the core argument behind organising cyber safety into a repeatable rhythm?
options: Repetition makes cyber safety unnecessarily complicated
Small, consistent habits repeated regularly are more sustainable and effective than a single, one-time effort
A single strong setup is always sufficient regardless of habits
Rhythm and repetition have no bearing on actual security outcomes
questions.explanation:
The central argument of this capstone module is that consistency and repetition, not one-time perfection, are what
actually sustain long-term cyber safety.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the recommended approach to teaching children the basics of this checklist?
options: Expect children to independently learn every aspect without guidance
Guide children through age-appropriate versions of the checklist, especially core daily habits like never sharing OTPs
Assume children don't need any cybersecurity guidance at all
Only discuss cyber safety with children after they experience a problem
questions.explanation:
Core habits like never sharing OTPs apply to everyone, and guiding children through age-appropriate versions of the fuller
checklist helps build safe habits early.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the purpose of including a "Suggested Infographics" section, like a master checklist poster,
in this module?
options: To make the handbook visually appealing with no practical function
To provide a memorable, at-a-glance reference tool summarising the full daily/weekly/monthly/as-needed routine
To replace the need for reading the actual content
To serve only as decoration for the PDF version
questions.explanation:
A one-page master checklist poster is designed to serve as a practical, easy-to-reference summary of the habits covered
throughout the module.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "reviewing new social media follower/connection requests" is placed under weekly
rather than daily habits?
options: It requires the same effort as verifying a UPI payment, so it must be daily
Reviewing periodically at a weekly cadence balances staying vigilant without requiring constant daily attention
Follower requests are irrelevant to cyber safety
This task should only be performed once per year
questions.explanation:
Weekly review is frequent enough to catch suspicious follower activity without requiring the constant daily attention
reserved for higher-frequency risks.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "reporting harassment" and "calling 1930 for fraud" are grouped under the same "as-
needed" category despite being very different situations?
options: Because they are actually identical actions
Because both are triggered by an actual incident occurring, rather than following a fixed calendar schedule
Because both require exactly the same helpline number
Because neither requires any evidence or documentation
questions.explanation:
Despite addressing different problems, both actions share the trait of being incident-triggered rather than scheduled,
which is why they fall under "as-needed."

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the intended real-world benefit of this module's Daily/Weekly/Monthly/As-Needed
structure?
options: It has no practical benefit beyond organising information

It turns nine modules of knowledge into a small number of sustainable habits that are easier to actually follow long-
term
It is intended only for IT professionals
It replaces the need to understand any of the underlying concepts
questions.explanation:
The structure's real value lies in converting broad knowledge into a manageable, realistic set of habits that people can
actually sustain over time.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the recommended response to receiving a threatening call claiming to be the "cyber crime
cell" itself?
options: Comply immediately since it claims official authority
Recognise it as a likely scam and disconnect, then report it yourself via cybercrime.gov.in or 1930 if needed
Share personal banking details to "verify" your innocence
Ignore it completely without any further action
questions.explanation:
Genuine cyber crime authorities do not operate this way; recognising the scam and reporting it independently is the
correct response.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "locking your device screen when stepping away" qualifies as a high-frequency daily
habit?
options: It only matters in high-security government offices
It's a quick, frequent action relevant to nearly every use of your device throughout the day
It should only be done once, when a device is first purchased
It has no real bearing on security
questions.explanation:
Because device use is constant throughout the day, locking the screen each time you step away is naturally a very
frequent, daily-level habit.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the intended message behind the phrase "small habits, repeated consistently, are what
actually keep you safe"?
options: Complex, one-time technical solutions are more important than habits
Consistent, simple habits sustained over time provide more real protection than a single advanced technical measure
Habits have no measurable impact on cyber safety outcomes
Only expensive security tools can provide meaningful protection
questions.explanation:
This phrase captures the module's central philosophy: sustainable, repeated small actions outperform relying solely on
one-time technical fixes.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the intended scope of the "as-needed" category regarding data breaches?
options: Data breach reporting should occur on a fixed monthly schedule regardless of actual events
Filing a complaint with the Data Protection Board is triggered specifically when a suspected breach occurs
Data breaches are not covered anywhere in this checklist
Data breach reporting is only relevant to large corporations
questions.explanation:
Like other as-needed actions, reporting a suspected data breach is triggered by the actual event occurring, not by a
routine calendar-based schedule.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why this module avoids introducing entirely new cyber threats not covered in Modules 1–9?
options: New threats are always more important than habit-building

Its purpose is specifically to consolidate and operationalise existing knowledge into sustainable habits, not introduce
new content
There are no other cyber threats worth mentioning
This module is meant to replace all previous modules entirely
questions.explanation:
As a capstone module, its role is to synthesise and make practical everything already covered, rather than introduce
unrelated new material.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the recommended cadence for checking "new app installs and their permissions"?
options: Daily
Weekly
Only once, when the phone is first purchased
Never✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation:
Reviewing new app installs and their permissions weekly ensures newly added risks are caught promptly without
requiring constant daily attention.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "updating weak or reused passwords, starting with email" is placed under the monthly
cadence?
options: Passwords should be changed every single day regardless of circumstances
A monthly cadence allows for a deeper, more thorough review than would be practical daily or weekly
Password updates have no place in any cadence
Only businesses need to update passwords periodically
questions.explanation:
Reviewing and strengthening passwords is a more substantial task suited to a monthly rhythm, rather than requiring
impractical daily attention.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the guidance around a family's shared "cyber safety day"?
options: It has no practical value for households
It encourages families to review the checklist together and assign shared responsibilities periodically
It should be observed only by IT professionals within the family
It replaces the need for any individual daily habits
questions.explanation:
A shared family cyber safety day helps reinforce the checklist collectively, encouraging accountability and awareness
across the household.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the recommended posture toward "as-needed" habits before an actual incident occurs?
options: Ignore them entirely until something goes wrong
Know them in advance so you don't hesitate or waste time when an actual incident occurs
Memorise them only after an incident has already happened
As-needed habits require no advance preparation at all
questions.explanation:
Knowing your as-needed steps in advance means you can act immediately and confidently rather than losing valuable
time figuring out what to do during a real incident.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the reasoning behind linking this module's habits back to specific earlier modules (e.g.,
"Modules 1, 3, 4")?
options: The cross-references serve no practical purpose
They help learners see how the practical checklist connects back to the detailed concepts learned earlier in the category
They indicate which modules should be skipped
They are included purely for decorative purposes
questions.explanation:
The cross-references reinforce learning by showing how each practical habit ties back to the more detailed concepts
covered in specific earlier modules.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the appropriate response to noticing a family member has never reviewed their app
permissions?
options: Assume it's not important since nothing has gone wrong yet
Encourage them to begin a monthly review habit, since starting late is still valuable
Take over their device entirely without their involvement
Wait for an incident before discussing it with them
questions.explanation:
Encouraging the habit to begin now, regardless of past neglect, extends meaningful protection going forward for that
family member.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "verifying payee names" and "locking your screen" are considered higher-frequency
habits than "auditing app permissions"?
options: There is no meaningful difference in frequency between these habits
The former are tied to actions performed many times daily, while permission audits require deeper, less frequent review
Auditing app permissions should actually be done more often than verifying payee names
Frequency has no bearing on how habits are categorised in this framework
questions.explanation:
The cadence framework matches habit frequency to how often the underlying action naturally occurs and how much
depth of review it requires.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the intended tone of this capstone module compared to the earlier modules in the
category?
options: It is more technical and detailed than any previous module
It is more practical and action-oriented, translating prior knowledge into a simple, repeatable routine
It focuses exclusively on advanced legal provisions
It contains no reference to real-life scenarios at all
questions.explanation:
This module intentionally shifts focus toward practical application, turning the detailed knowledge from earlier modules
into an actionable daily routine.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the four cadences used to organise habits in this module?
options: Daily
Weekly
Yearly
As-Needed✅ Correct Answer: Option C
questions.explanation:
The four cadences used are Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and As-Needed — "Yearly" is not one of the categories, though the
module references annual national campaigns separately.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is its ultimate stated goal?
options: To introduce a completely new set of unrelated cybersecurity threats
To turn nine modules of knowledge into habits simple enough to sustain for life
To replace the need for any government cybersecurity agency
To provide entertainment value with no practical application
questions.explanation: Official JanGyan verified citizen concept.
